title: Islamic Banking Service Landscape
note: Source of truth for the ISOLATED Islamic banking landscape. Modelled in the BIAN service-domain style but Shariah-native: no interest-bearing constructs — profit-sharing (Mudarabah/Musharakah), cost-plus sale (Murabaha), leasing (Ijara), and fee-based (Ujrah/Wakala) structures instead. Completely separate from the conventional landscape: own repos (isb-*), own template, own namespaces.

serviceDomains.name: Shariah Supervisory Board Directory

fields.name: mandateId
fields.description: Primary key of the mandate.

fields.name: boardId
fields.description: The governance organ this mandate sits on.

fields.name: organUnit
fields.description: The five organs AAOIFI GS 1 (Revised 2024) with GS 8 / GS 9 / GS 11 distinguishes. A fatwa reference and an audit trail attach to one of these, never to 'the bank'.

fields.name: institutionLei
fields.description: LEI of the institution the mandate is held at. Needed to make concurrent-mandate disclosure meaningful.

fields.name: isFinanceWindow
fields.description: The institution is an Islamic finance window of a conventional bank — AAOIFI GS 23 (issued Jan 2026) applies different governance expectations.

fields.name: appointmentAuthority
fields.description: AAOIFI GS 19 governs appointment and composition; which organ appoints is jurisdictional, so it is recorded, not assumed.

fields.name: regulatorApprovalRequired
fields.description: Per-jurisdiction. Recorded on the mandate because the directory is the only place that knows the institution's jurisdiction.

fields.name: supersedesMandateId
fields.description: Renewal chain. A renewed term is a NEW mandate row, never an edit of termEndsOn — the directory has to be able to answer 'was this person a member on date D'.

fields.name: policyPortWired
fields.description: False means every cross-domain rule on this record degraded to flag. See conventions.ruleScope.

fields.name: mayActAlone
fields.description: AAOIFI GS 18 governs the Shariah decision-making process; whether one member may rule alone is a recorded delegation, never an implicit default.

fields.name: minimumMemberCount
fields.description: A per-jurisdiction PARAMETER, not a constant. The commonly quoted minimum of three was not confirmed from a primary AAOIFI GS 19 text in the research behind this design — see uncertain.

rules.note: An out-of-order term makes 'was this member active on date D' unanswerable, which is the directory's only job.
A mandate cannot be ACTIVE outside its own term.

rules.assert: (cr.status == 'ACTIVE' && cr.regulatorApprovalRequired) implies cr.regulatorApprovalReference is not null
rules.note: Where the jurisdiction requires regulator approval of an SSB appointment, an ACTIVE mandate without the reference is an unevidenced claim.

rules.assert: count(BoardCompositionPolicy) == 1 && count(MandateTerm where endsOn > startsOn) == count(MandateTerm)
rules.note: Every mandate is evaluated against exactly one recorded composition policy; term rows obey the same ordering as the control record.

rules.assert: count(mandate where boardId == cr.boardId && status == 'ACTIVE') >= BoardCompositionPolicy.minimumMemberCount
rules.note: Quorum/composition is jurisdictional and the count spans rows, not one record. Flag, never reject — refusing a termination because it breaks quorum would make an unlawful board unfixable.

rules.assert: (BoardCompositionPolicy.competingInstitutionMandatePermitted == false) implies count(ConcurrentMandate where isCompetingInstitution == true) == 0
rules.note: Cross-membership at a competing institution is restricted in some jurisdictions and disclosed in others. Flagged and recorded; the determination is the regulator's.

rules.assert: cr.status in ['TERMINATED','EXPIRED'] implies cr.terminationReason is not null

rules.note: A renewal is a new row; the superseded row must already be closed, so two ACTIVE mandates can never overlap for the same seat.

rules.assert: no in-place update of mandateId, memberPartyId, boardId, termStartsOn, termEndsOn or appointmentReference once cr.status != 'NOMINATED'
rules.note: DESIGN.md §5.8. The directory is the evidence a fatwa's signatory was authorised; rewriting it destroys that evidence.

Whether a member of the internal Shariah audit organ may concurrently hold an SSB mandate. Jurisdictional; recorded via organUnit plus Independence Assessment and flagged in the audit domain, never rejected here.
Cross-membership caps and the definition of a 'competing institution'. Recorded as policy parameters with a named source; the catalog supplies no default.

serviceDomains.name: Fatwa And Ruling Repository

fields.name: retroactive
fields.description: True where effectiveFrom precedes issuedOn — which happens on Shariah non-compliance remediation. Requires a justification rather than being silently allowed.

fields.name: rulingType
fields.description: METHOD_SELECTION and POLICY_PARAMETER are what let Income Purification and Zakat Calculation point at an authority instead of hardcoding a formula.

fields.name: basisSchoolNote
fields.description: Free text, deliberately NOT an enum of madhhabs. Attributing a ruling to a school of law is a scholarly claim this code must not encode as a closed list.

fields.name: jurisdiction
fields.description: Null means not jurisdiction-scoped.

fields.name: documentDigest
fields.description: SHA-256 of the signed ruling document. This is what makes the repository evidence rather than a note.

fields.name: primaryTextObtained
fields.description: False means the citation came from a secondary source. This is the field that stops the estate laundering commentary into authority.

rules.note: A ruling with no concurring signatory is not a ruling. AAOIFI GS 18.
Every signatory must have held an ACTIVE mandate on the issuance date. Needs the directory's state, so it generates a PolicyPort; while unwired it flags and policyPortWired records that it did.

rules.assert: cr.retroactive == (cr.effectiveFrom < cr.issuedOn) && (cr.retroactive implies cr.retroactiveJustification is not null)
rules.note: Retroactive effect is real in remediation but must be declared and justified, never inferred from the dates.

rules.assert: no in-place update of documentDigest, documentUri, issuedOn, resolutionNumber or decisionBasis once cr.status == 'ISSUED'
rules.note: An ISSUED ruling is immutable. A change is a new ruling that supersedes it, plus an Amendment History row carrying the prior digest. DESIGN.md §5.8.

rules.assert: cr.status == 'SUPERSEDED' implies (cr.supersededByRulingId is not null && cr.effectiveTo is not null)

rules.note: Supersession is a closed two-sided link, so 'which ruling governs date D' has exactly one answer.

rules.assert: cr.status == 'WITHDRAWN' implies cr.withdrawalReason is not null

rules.note: A ruling that sets a screening criterion, a policy parameter or a computation method with no cited standard is unsourced. It is recorded and flagged rather than rejected — an SSB may rule on its own authority — but it never passes silently.

rules.assert: all CitedStandard: (body in ['AAOIFI','IFSB'] implies (standardCode is not null && clause is not null))
rules.note: A bare 'per AAOIFI' is not a citation. Code and clause or nothing.
Secondary-source citations are permitted and labelled. The flag is the label.
The dissent flag must match the signatory rows; a hidden dissent is the one thing a ruling repository must not be able to do.

shariah.contractTypeNote: Not a contract. This is the authority register every other domain in the estate cites — a rule, a screening criterion, a zakat method and a purification formula each point at a rulingId here, which is how the code stops manufacturing authority.
shariah.reviewStatus: UNREVIEWED — requires named Shariah board sign-off

standards.title: Shari'ah Decision-Making Process
standards.note: The signatory, delegation and dissent model.

standards.title: Guiding Principles for Effective Supervision of Shariah Governance
standards.note: Principle 9 refers to approved screening criteria — the SCREENING_CRITERIA ruling type exists so those criteria have an authority to point at.

shariah.review: UNREVIEWED — requires named Shariah board sign-off

uncertain: The required quorum and voting threshold for a valid ruling. Modelled through Ruling Signatory positions and the Delegated Authority BQ of the SSB directory, with no threshold asserted, because the primary GS 18 / GS 20 texts were not obtained.
Whether a dissenting opinion must be published. The repository can record and digest it; whether it must be disclosed is a GS 21 / jurisdictional question left open.
Madhhab attribution is deliberately free text. Any closed enum here would be the code taking a scholarly position.
Retroactive effect. Modelled as a declared, justified flag. Whether a retroactive Shariah ruling may validate or void a settled transaction is not something this catalog decides.

serviceDomains.name: Shariah Compliance Review

fields.name: productScope
fields.description: e.g. ISLAMIC_CREDIT_CARD. Carried because the only regulation that mandates transaction screening mandates it for one product.

fields.name: policyVersion
fields.description: Monotonic. Recorded on the decision so the decision is replayable against the exact rule set that produced it.

fields.name: gateMode
fields.description: Per-jurisdiction, per-product. DISABLED still writes a case with decision NOT_APPLICABLE — a silent gate is worse than an absent one.

fields.name: mandateBasis
fields.description: Why this gate is running at all. REGULATION is correct for BD/ISLAMIC_CREDIT_CARD and, on the evidence behind this design, for nothing else.

fields.name: mandateBasisReference
fields.description: Required when mandateBasis == REGULATION. e.g. 'Bangladesh Bank IBRPD Circular No. 01, 27 Sep 2026, s.45 Bank Company Act 1991'.

fields.name: decision
fields.description: Exactly three outcomes plus the disabled case. There is no 'HALAL' value and there never will be.

fields.name: decisionReasonCode
fields.description: Names the criterionId that fired, or the policy's declared defaultOutcome. Never free text.

fields.name: appliedByRulingId
fields.description: The SSB ruling behind the criterion. Mandatory for a BLOCK.

fields.name: evidenceQuality
fields.description: An MCC or an ISO 20022 purpose code is a PROXY: a supermarket selling alcohol carries one code, and purpose codes are customer-supplied and absent on most domestic rails. The estate may never present a PROXY match as a determination.

fields.name: customerVisibleReason
fields.description: Required for a BLOCK. Blocking a payment on religious grounds without a reason the customer can see is itself a consumer-protection problem.

fields.name: supersedesCaseId
fields.description: A changed outcome is a new case. Decisions are never edited.

fields.name: interactionId
fields.description: x-fapi-interaction-id, correlation only. Never trusted as identity (DESIGN.md §5.6).

fields.name: defaultOutcome
fields.description: Deny-by-default is CONFIGURABLE, not assumed. A deployment that defaults to BLOCK in a jurisdiction where screening is not required will break legitimate payments.

fields.name: selectorType
fields.description: MCC is ISO 18245; ISO20022_PURPOSE is the 4-character Purpose / ExtendedPurpose element. Both are proxies by construction — see rule ISB-GOV-SCR-04.

fields.name: inputHashed
fields.description: Counterparty identifiers are hashed before they reach the trace; the flag says which form the row holds, so a replay knows what it can and cannot re-derive.

fields.name: recognisedAsIncome
fields.description: Must be false. Present as a field so the invariant is assertable and auditable rather than implicit.

fields.name: checkCode
fields.description: AAOIFI SS 8 §3/2 (possession and risk transfer before onward sale), SS 3 §2/5/3 (set-off currency), SS 13 §9/6 (nothing charged to the IAH pool), SS 47 §5 (no accrual on arrears), SS 8 §4/3 and SS 47 §9 (fixed total price disclosed), SS 3 §2/1/4 and §2/1/8 (recovery costs and charity undertaking as separate non-income lines).

rules.assert: cr.decision == 'BLOCK' implies (cr.appliedByRulingId is not null && cr.customerVisibleReason is not null)
rules.note: The estate may never block a payment on religious grounds without a recorded, SSB-approved rule AND a reason the customer can read.

testVectors.name: block without ruling is refused
testVectors.given: decision=BLOCK, appliedByRulingId=null, customerVisibleReason='Merchant category not permitted'

testVectors.name: block without customer reason is refused

rules.assert: cr.gateMode == 'ENFORCING' implies (cr.mandateBasis in ['REGULATION','ISSUER_PRACTICE'] && (cr.mandateBasis == 'REGULATION' implies cr.mandateBasisReference is not null))
rules.note: This is the one-jurisdiction fact made executable. An enforcing gate must name why it enforces. On the evidence behind this design, only BD + ISLAMIC_CREDIT_CARD can honestly answer REGULATION.

testVectors.name: BD islamic credit card enforces on regulation
testVectors.given: jurisdiction=BD, productScope=ISLAMIC_CREDIT_CARD, gateMode=ENFORCING, mandateBasis=REGULATION, mandateBasisReference='Bangladesh Bank IBRPD Circular No. 01, 27 Sep 2026'

testVectors.name: enforcing with NOT_REQUIRED basis is refused
MY issuer practice may enforce without a regulation reference

rules.assert: exists(ScreeningPolicy where policyId == cr.policyId && version == cr.policyVersion && status == 'ACTIVE' && effectiveFrom <= cr.decidedAt && (effectiveTo is null || effectiveTo > cr.decidedAt))
rules.note: No decision may exist without the exact policy version that produced it being present and effective at decision time. This is what makes the rule set DATA: a decision the code could have reached without a row is refused.

An MCC or a purpose code is a coarse proxy — one code per mixed merchant, customer-supplied, absent on most domestic rails. Recording such a match as DIRECT evidence would turn a proxy into a determination.

rules.assert: cr.firedCriterionId is not null || cr.decisionReasonCode == concat('POLICY_DEFAULT:', cr.policyId)
rules.note: Every decision names the criterion that fired or the policy default. There is no third source of a decision, and in particular no code path.

rules.assert: count(Referral where outcome is null && slaDueAt < now()) == 0
rules.note: An unresolved referral past SLA is an operational signal, not a reason to refuse the write.
A disabled gate still writes a case. The alternative — no row at all — makes 'was screening on' unanswerable after the fact.
Shariah non-compliant income never enters P&L. AAOIFI SS 13 §9/6 and GS 9.

rules.assert: all NonComplianceEvent: (quarantinedAmount is null || (fundingAccountContractType not in ['Mudarabah','Musharakah','Wakala'] && segregatedLiabilityAccountRef is not null))
rules.note: Quarantined SNC income sits in a segregated liability and is never funded from an investment-account-holder pool. AAOIFI SS 13 §9/6: the Mudarib may not make a gift or charitable donation out of Mudarabah funds.

rules.assert: all NonComplianceEvent: (charityChannelledAmount is null || (charityChannelledAmount.currency == quarantinedAmount.currency && charityChannelledAmount.minor <= quarantinedAmount.minor && charityChannelledAmount.minor >= 0))
rules.note: Integer minor units, one currency, never more channelled than quarantined.

rules.assert: all NonComplianceEvent: (determination != 'PENDING' implies (determinedByRulingId is not null && determinedAt is not null))
rules.note: The service records and routes; the SSB determines. A determination with no ruling behind it is the code pretending to be a scholar.

rules.assert: no in-place update of decision, decisionReasonCode, firedCriterionId, policyVersion, criteriaListVersion, decidedAt or evidenceQuality once the case row exists
rules.note: A changed outcome is a new case with supersedesCaseId set. DESIGN.md §5.8 — append-only for every Shariah non-compliance finding.

rules.assert: cr.supersedesCaseId is null || status(cr.supersedesCaseId) is not null

rules.note: A decision may not cite a withdrawn or not-yet-effective ruling. Needs the repository's state; degrades to flag while the PolicyPort is unwired.

rules.assert: all ContractIntegrityCheck: (citedStandardCode is not null && citedClause is not null)
rules.note: A contract-integrity check with no clause behind it is an opinion in a boolean.

rules.assert: all ScreeningCriterion: (outcome == 'BLOCK' implies (approvedByRulingId is not null && customerVisibleReason is not null))
rules.note: The BLOCK requirement is enforced where the criterion is authored, not only where it fires.

rules.assert: count(ScreeningCriterion group by policyId, precedence having count > 1) == 0
rules.note: Ambiguous precedence makes a decision non-replayable.

shariah.contractTypeNote: The gate assesses contracts; it is not one. affectedContractType on a non-compliance event carries the contract under assessment.
shariah.reviewStatus: UNREVIEWED — requires named Shariah board sign-off. This is the single most consequential block in the estate: every criterion row, every default outcome and every contract-integrity check code below is a developer's reading of a standard until a named SSB signs it.

standards.title: Guidelines on Islamic Credit Card Operations of Banks
standards.note: Dated 27 September 2026 (12 Ashwin 1433), issued under s.45 Bank Company Act 1991, in force immediately. §3 requires that all products, contracts, transactions, fees, charges and operational processes be conducted in accordance with Shariah. THE ONLY central-bank instrument found that puts transaction-level Shariah screening in regulation. CAVEAT recorded in the research: the annexed guidelines in the published PDF are image-only, so the MCC detail (alcohol, gambling, conventional insurance, pork processing, interest-based financial services) comes from press reporting of the circular, not from extracted text.

standards.title: Guiding Principles for Effective Supervision of Shariah Governance
standards.note: Adopted Jul 2025. Principle 8 (outsourcing does not move responsibility — hence a vendor verdict is data with a source and asOf, never an authority), Principle 9 ('approved screening criteria' — hence ScreeningCriterion.approvedByRulingId), Principles 9-10 (the institution records and routes a non-compliance; it does not self-absolve).

standards.note: Recovery costs and the charity undertaking as separate non-income lines; set-off in the same currency or at the prevailing rate. Amendments adopted at Board meeting No. 38, 26-28 June 2014.

standards.title: Murabaha
standards.note: Possession and risk transfer before onward sale; fixed total sale price disclosed.
No accrual on arrears; mandatory disclosure of the profit calculation.

standards.title: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds)
standards.note: The business-activity and financial-ratio screens behind selectorType ACTIVITY_RATIO. The widely quoted 30/30/5 thresholds come ONLY from vendor and commentary sources in the research behind this design; the primary text was not obtained. No threshold is hardcoded anywhere in this entry — thresholds are ScreeningCriterion rows with a rulingId.

standards.title: Merchant Category Codes
standards.note: The MCC selector's value space.

standards.title: Purpose / ExtendedPurpose
standards.note: 4-character Purpose; ExtendedPurpose is international-only in the Bahrain PISP spec and absent on most domestic rails.

shariah.review: UNREVIEWED — requires named Shariah board sign-off

uncertain: The Bangladesh circular's MCC list. The published PDF's annex is image-only; the categories named in press reporting were not extracted from the instrument. The catalog therefore ships NO MCC rows — only the table that holds them and the rule that a row needs a rulingId.
AAOIFI SS 21's 30/30/5 thresholds. Secondary sources only. Modelled as data, never as a constant.
Whether a REFER may time out to ALLOW. No source supports either answer, so the catalog makes an unresolved referral a flag and leaves the outcome null rather than inventing a timeout policy.
Whether a transaction already executed and later found non-compliant must be reversed, voided or merely purified. The determination enum records all three; the code never picks.

The contract-integrity check codes are a developer's enumeration of clause readings. Each carries its cited clause so a reviewer can disagree with a specific line rather than with a black box. Several (NO_GUARANTEED_OBLIGATION_ON_IAH_POOL, CHARITY_UNDERTAKING_SEPARATE_FROM_INCOME) are the ones most likely to be wrong in detail.

Deny-by-default. The catalog deliberately refuses to choose: defaultOutcome is a required policy field with no default value. A deny-by-default gate in a jurisdiction where screening is not required will refuse lawful payments, and that is itself a consumer-protection problem.
serviceDomains.gateHonesty: THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL COMPONENT IN THE ESTATE, AND THE EASIEST TO OVERSTATE. Transaction-level Shariah screening is a regulatory requirement in exactly ONE jurisdiction for ONE product: Bangladesh Bank IBRPD Circular No. 01 of 27 September 2026, 'Guidelines on Islamic Credit Card Operations of Banks'. Everywhere else — including the Malaysian MCC blocking practised by Maybank Islamic Ikhwan, AmBank Islamic and Bank Islam Card-i — it is ISSUER PRACTICE, not regulation. That fact is not a README footnote here: it is the mandateBasis enum on every screening policy, it is enforced by rule ISB-GOV-SCR-02, and a gate running in ENFORCING mode without a recorded basis is rejected. The rule set itself is DATA (ScreeningPolicy + ScreeningCriterion rows, per jurisdiction, per product scope, effective-dated, each approved by a rulingId). There is no screening logic in code — the generated rules component evaluates rows and cannot evaluate anything else.

serviceDomains.name: Shariah Audit

fields.name: auditorMandateId
fields.description: Set where the auditor also holds a governance mandate — which is what makes the independence flag checkable.

fields.name: opinionRulingId
fields.description: The SSB report itself is a ruling in the repository (AAOIFI GS 21), not a PDF in a bucket.

fields.name: auditingFramework
fields.description: AAOIFI SOAA 1 'Framework of Auditing' and SOAA 4 'Auditing Requirements for Assessing Compliance with Shari'ah' were issued Jan 2026; AGN 3 'Illustrative Auditor's Report' on 8 Nov 2026.

fields.name: selectionSeed
fields.description: Explicit PCG seed so a statistical sample is replayable (DESIGN.md D9 uses the same discipline for the seed universe). A sample nobody can redraw is not evidence.

fields.name: soaaAuditConfirmed
fields.description: AGEB Statement 1/2025 grants the external Shariah audit exemption only where the institution is audited under AAOIFI's SOAAs. Claiming the exemption without this is the obvious abuse.

fields.name: correlatedSncEventId
fields.description: Set when the finding raised a non-compliance event in isb-shariah-compliance-review. Its absence on a SHARIAH_NON_COMPLIANCE finding is the dangling-finding case rule ISB-GOV-AUD-04 catches.

fields.name: verifiedByEngagementId
fields.description: Closed by a LATER engagement, not by the owner. This is what makes 'remediation tracking' more than a status field.

rules.assert: cr.opinionType != 'NOT_ISSUED' implies (cr.reportIssuedOn is not null && cr.fieldworkCompletedOn is not null && count(AuditEvidence) >= 1)
rules.note: An opinion with no evidence row and no fieldwork date is an assertion, not an audit.

rules.assert: cr.sampleSize <= cr.populationSize && (cr.samplingMethod == 'FULL_POPULATION' implies cr.sampleSize == cr.populationSize) && (cr.samplingMethod == 'STATISTICAL' implies cr.selectionSeed is not null) && count(AuditSample) == cr.sampleSize
rules.note: A statistical sample nobody can redraw, or a sample whose row count disagrees with its declared size, is not evidence.

rules.assert: count(AuditFinding where findingType == 'SHARIAH_NON_COMPLIANCE' && correlatedSncEventId is null) == 0
rules.note: A non-compliance finding that never became an SNC event in the compliance-review domain is a finding that will never be quarantined or channelled. Flagged loudly; not rejected, because the auditor must be able to record the finding before the workflow catches up.

rules.assert: cr.externalAuditExemptionClaimed implies (cr.externalAuditExemptionReference is not null && cr.soaaAuditConfirmed == true)
rules.note: AGEB Statement 1/2025 grants the external Shariah audit exemption only where the institution is audited under AAOIFI's SOAAs. Claiming it without naming the instrument and confirming the SOAA audit is the obvious abuse.
Whether an internal Shariah auditor may concurrently sit on the SSB is jurisdictional (GS 11 against GS 19/20). Recorded and flagged; the catalog does not rule on it.

rules.assert: all AuditFinding: (severity in ['CRITICAL','HIGH'] implies count(Remediation where findingId == findingId) >= 1)
all Remediation: (status == 'DONE' implies (completedOn is not null && verifiedByEngagementId is not null)) && (status == 'ACCEPTED_RISK' implies acceptedRiskRulingId is not null)
rules.note: A remediation closes when a later engagement verifies it, or when a ruling accepts the risk. The owner cannot close their own finding.

rules.assert: all Remediation: (status == 'OVERDUE') == (dueOn < now() && status not in ['DONE','ACCEPTED_RISK'])
no in-place update of findingId, findingType, severity, raisedOn, citedStandardCode or citedClause once an AuditFinding row exists; no DELETE of any AuditFinding, Remediation or AuditEvidence row
rules.note: DESIGN.md §5.8. A deleted finding is the defect this invariant exists to prevent.

serviceDomains.name: Income Purification

fields.name: methodCode
fields.description: Published sources genuinely conflict on the purification formula (per-share impermissible income against a ratio applied to received dividends plus realised gains) and on whether capital gains are purified at all. The method is therefore an SSB CHOICE recorded with a ruling, never a default.

fields.name: methodRulingId
fields.description: Required. There is no default method, because choosing one in code would be the developer issuing a fatwa.

fields.name: impermissibleRatio
fields.description: Exact num/den. 0 <= num <= den.

fields.name: roundingPolicy
fields.description: Required, no default. Rounding a religious due is a Shariah choice, not an engineering preference. Recorded on every row so the figure is reproducible.

fields.name: capitalGainsIncluded
fields.description: Sources disagree. Recorded per entry rather than assumed.

fields.name: recognisedAsIncome
fields.description: Must be false.

fields.name: derivedRatio
fields.description: num = impermissibleRevenue.minor, den = totalRevenue.minor. The ratio is DERIVED from two integers, never typed in as a percentage.

fields.name: shareCount
fields.description: For PER_SHARE. Integer count; the per-share figure is amount-per-share as money, never a float.

fields.name: purposeCode

serviceDomains.name: Zakat Calculation

fields.name: baseMethod
fields.description: AAOIFI FAS 9 permitted both. FAS 39 'Financial reporting for Zakah' (from exposure draft F5/2019 v5.1, 8 July 2020) records that the Shariah standard only provided net assets and DROPS net invested funds. NET_INVESTED_FUNDS therefore needs a ruling and a legacy note.

fields.name: calendarBasis
fields.description: The obligation remains attached to the Hijri calendar; a solar basis is a reporting convenience that changes the rate.

fields.name: hawlDays
fields.description: 354 for a full lunar year per AAOIFI SS 35 as cited by ZATCA. A lunar year is 354 or 355 days in practice, so this is recorded, checked loosely and flagged — never silently normalised.

fields.name: zakatRate
fields.description: Exact. 1/40 on HIJRI_LUNAR; 365/14160 on GREGORIAN_SOLAR (= 1/40 * 365/354). Never 0.025 and never 2.5.

fields.name: zakatRateRulingId
fields.description: Required only to override the standard rate for the recorded calendar basis.

fields.name: nisabMassMilligrams
fields.description: Integer milligrams. 595 g silver = 595000. The gold figure diverges across sources (85 g against 87.48 g) and the silver figure across sources too (595 g against 612.36 g); only the silver 595 g is traceable to a primary citation, so this is a SOURCED PARAMETER, never a constant in code.

fields.name: spotPriceMassBasisMilligrams
fields.description: What mass metalSpotPrice is the price OF (e.g. 1000000 for a price per kilogram). Makes step 1 a pure integer ratio.

fields.name: roundingPolicy
fields.description: Required, no default.

fields.name: payerRole
fields.description: Required. The research is explicit: state plainly whether the bank pays on the customer's behalf or only informs. An assessment that does not say is a misleading document.

fields.name: advisoryOnly
fields.description: True for a customer assessment presented as a computation with visible inputs rather than as a determination of the customer's religious obligation.

fields.name: inclusionRatio
fields.description: Exact. 1/1 for fully zakatable, 0/1 for excluded, and a partial ratio where the SSB rules one applies.

fields.name: divergenceNote
fields.description: e.g. 'Gold nisab is quoted as 85 g and as 87.48 g; silver as 595 g and as 612.36 g. Only silver 595 g (200 dirhams, AAOIFI SS 35 p.874 as cited by ZATCA) is traceable to a primary citation here.'

serviceDomains.arithmetic:
EXACT INTEGER ONLY, four steps, each reproducible from the stored row:
  1. nisabValueMinor   = round(metalSpotPrice.minor * nisabMassMilligrams / spotPriceMassBasisMilligrams, roundingPolicy)
  2. netZakatableMinor = zakatableBaseAmount.minor - deductibleLiabilitiesAmount.minor
  3. nisabMet          = netZakatableMinor >= nisabValueMinor
  4. zakatDueMinor     = nisabMet ? round(netZakatableMinor * zakatRate.num / zakatRate.den, roundingPolicy) : 0
The rate is an EXACT ratio: 1/40 on a lunar (Hijri) basis. The often-quoted solar figure of ~2.577% is exactly 1/40 * 365/354 = 365/14160, so it too is an exact ratio and is stored as one — a float here would quietly change a religious due. Masses are int64 MILLIGRAMS (595 g = 595000 mg), so no decimal mass ever appears.

It receives late-payment charity (AAOIFI SS 3 §2/1/8), quarantined Shariah non-compliant income, income-purification proceeds and voluntary sadaqah — and the permitted USE of each differs by its SOURCE. Every inflow is therefore source-tagged, a PermittedUsePolicy row says what each source may fund, and no outflow may draw more from a source bucket than that bucket received. Zakat is explicitly NOT here: it has its own fund, its own categories and its own service.

uncertain: AAOIFI has no standalone Wadiah Shariah Standard in the research set. The yad dhamanah / yad amanah split is predominantly Bank Negara Malaysia and wider Malaysian practice; AAOIFI SS 19 §10/1/1 would reclassify a usable Wadiah balance as qard regardless of the label. ISB-WAD-03 is therefore derived, not cited, and an SSB may reject the two-value enum entirely.

Whether YAD_AMANAH belongs in a retail deposits product line at all is a product question I cannot settle: a pure-trust account whose funds the bank may not use is closer to custody than to banking. It is modelled because the master catalog calls this a 'Custody Account', and it is the honest reason capitalAtRisk is not hard-coded false.

uncertain: This control record is data-identical to the Wadiah Safekeeping Account record apart from the contract label, the Wadiah type enum and set-off. I report that as a finding rather than inventing a difference: under AAOIFI SS 19 §10/1/1 a usable Wadiah balance IS a qard, so two separate service domains may be the right PRODUCT decomposition and the wrong DATA decomposition. Collapsing them into one domain with a contractType discriminator would remove a service and a repo; that call belongs to the owner and the SSB, not to me.

ISB-QRD-05 cannot be fully enforced here. AAOIFI SS 3 §1 excludes insolvent debtors and §2/6 makes default a two-condition state (demand served AND insolvency not proven), but neither the demand record nor the insolvency determination lives in this domain. The generated guard can only check the contractual permission flag; the solvency precondition must be asserted by the financing domain that initiates the set-off.

Dormancy: a DORMANT status is modelled because dormancy fees are a real Shariah question (a dormancy fee must still be actual direct cost), but no standard in the research set fixes a dormancy period, so no threshold is in the catalog.

serviceDomains.name: Mudarabah Savings Account

fields.name: investmentAccountType
fields.note: AAOIFI SS 13 §5 / BNM PD 028-63 ¶25.2(b)(ii). A savings product is commingled and unrestricted; RESTRICTED belongs to the term domain, which carries an Investment Mandate behaviour qualifier.

fields.name: capitalAtRisk
fields.note: THE load-bearing field of this business area. Queryable, indexed, and read by the funds-confirmation path before any balance is disclosed.

fields.name: lossBearer
fields.note: AAOIFI SS 13 §8/7 and SS 45 §3/4 make ACCOUNT_HOLDER mandatory for Mudarabah. Not a configurable product option.

fields.name: fundsConfirmationSupported
fields.note: DESIGN.md §7: a CBPII funds confirmation against this account must REFUSE. FundsAvailable:true would be a false statement about a balance the bank does not guarantee.

fields.name: capitalProtection
fields.note: AAOIFI SS 45 §2 — protection is explicitly WIDER THAN and DISTINCT FROM guarantee. Protection does not make capitalAtRisk false.

fields.name: managerLiabilityBasis
fields.note: AAOIFI SS 13 §4/4, SS 45 §3/4 and §3/6 — the mudarib is not liable for loss except for breach of trust, misconduct, negligence or breach of terms, and unconditional liability may not be stipulated.

fields.name: balanceMinor
fields.note: the account holder's current attributable capital. Not a liability of the bank: AAOIFI FAS 45 classifies investment accounts as QUASI-EQUITY, not liabilities. The generated README must say so, because an IFRS-trained reader will assume otherwise.

fields.name: cumulativeCapitalLossBorneMinor
fields.note: how a capital LOSS is represented without a negative balance: losses are recorded here and reduce balanceMinor, bounded by MUDS-02. AAOIFI SS 13 §4/4 requires the model to be able to represent a negative capital movement.

fields.name: profitCalculationMethodRef
fields.note: AAOIFI SS 47 §9 makes disclosure of the method of profit calculation mandatory, including the right of the client to inquire about it. IFSB-30 ¶272/¶275 require it in a machine-readable, comparable form.

fields.name: poolWeightage
fields.note: exact. The pool weightage applied to this account's balance before the profit-sharing ratio.

fields.name: expectedProfitRateBasis
fields.note: AAOIFI SS 47 §7/2 — a minimum expected profit rate may be stipulated for deployment, but neither capital nor profit may be guaranteed. BNM ¶24.5 forbids any term indicating a guaranteed return.

fields.name: riskWarningAcknowledgedAt
fields.note: BNM PD 028-63 ¶25.2(i)-(j) — the 'NOT A DEPOSIT PRODUCT' disclaimer and the 'PRINCIPAL AND RETURNS ARE NOT GUARANTEED' warning. AAOIFI SS 38 §5/4/1 requires an explicit acceptance-confirmation step, so the timestamp is a Shariah artefact, not UX telemetry.

behaviourQualifiers.name: Profit Sharing Agreement

fields.name: effectiveTo
fields.note: null = open-ended

fields.name: psrIahShare
fields.note: a share of PROFIT. AAOIFI SS 13 §8/1 — distribution must be an agreed percentage of the profit, never a lump sum and never a percentage of the capital.

fields.name: contractualMaximumMudaribShare
fields.note: IFSB GN-3 fn.13 — a unilateral increase of the mudarib share above the contractual maximum is not permitted. The contractual share is a CEILING; the realised share may be lower, including zero if waived.

behaviourQualifiers.note: BIAN has no profit-sharing behaviour qualifier — it has no Islamic constructs at all. This BQ exists because AAOIFI SS 13 §8/3 makes the PSR effective-dated, versioned data rather than a static product attribute, and IFSB-30 ¶276 requires it to be declared IN ADVANCE.

fields.name: distributionType
fields.note: AAOIFI SS 13 §8/8 — an interim distribution is revised when actual or constructive valuation takes place. The revision is modelled as TWO postings (a reversal and a final), never an update in place.

fields.note: balanceMinor x days. Bounded in practice: 10^15 minor units x 366 days stays well inside int64, but the generated repository must still reject an input that would overflow rather than wrap.

behaviourQualifiers.note: BNM PD 028-63 ¶25.2 is the most concrete published field list for an Islamic investment-account disclosure; IFSB-30 ¶272–¶278 requires the same information in machine-readable form. This BQ is what the openbank-islamic sibling resource server serves.

AAOIFI SS 13 §8/7 — 'No profit can be recognised or claimed unless the capital of the Mudarabah is maintained intact.' Losses are carried forward and set against future profits.

AAOIFI SS 38 §5/4/1 (explicit acceptance confirmation)
IFSB-30 ¶276 (PSR declared in advance)
IFSB-31 Principle 9 (screening).

standards: AAOIFI SS 13 (Mudarabah, Revised) §1 Scope — expressly covers joint and special-purpose investment accounts administered on a Mudarabah basis, so SS 13 binds retail investment-account APIs.
AAOIFI SS 13 §4/4 — trust-based: the mudarib is not liable for losses except for breach of trust, misconduct, negligence or breach of terms.
AAOIFI SS 13 §8/1 — distribution must be an agreed percentage of PROFIT, not a lump sum and not a percentage of capital.
AAOIFI SS 13 §8/3 — the ratio is agreed at contract conclusion, may be changed by agreement, with a stated validity duration (hence effective-dated PSR rows).
AAOIFI SS 13 §8/5 — a stipulated lump sum for either party voids the Mudarabah.
AAOIFI SS 13 §8/7 — no profit may be recognised or claimed unless the capital is maintained intact.
AAOIFI SS 13 §8/8 — interim distribution on account is permitted but revised on actual or constructive valuation; neither time value nor discounting may be taken into account.

AAOIFI SS 45 (Protection of Capital and Investments) §2, §3/4, §3/6, §4/1/1, §4/2/4 — protection is distinct from guarantee; unconditional manager liability may not be stipulated; third-party protection requires administrative independence.

AAOIFI SS 47 (Rules for Calculating Profit) §7/2 and §9 — a minimum expected rate may be stipulated for deployment without guaranteeing capital or profit; the method of profit calculation must be disclosed.
AAOIFI FAS 45 — Quasi-equity (Including Investment Accounts), superseding FAS 27: investment accounts are quasi-equity, not liabilities.

IFSB GN-3 fn.12 (citing IFSB-2 ¶76) — the IIFS as mudarib may not absorb IAH investment losses except for misconduct or negligence. fn.13 — no unilateral increase of the mudarib share above the contractual maximum.

IFSB-30 Principle 18 ¶272, ¶275, ¶276 — IAH entitlement to the profit-calculation method, asset allocation, strategies and smoothing mechanics, in a comparable and readily accessible form; the PSR must be declared in advance.
IFSB-22 Table 7 / Template 10 — Unrestricted PSIA qualitative and quantitative disclosures.

BNM PD 028-63 ¶8.2, ¶13.1, ¶24.5, ¶25.2, ¶27.6 — no obligation to repay in full; profit-distribution terms; prohibition on deposit-like or guarantee-like terminology; the disclosure-sheet field list; 'declared rate of return' as the correct term for the realised figure.

uncertain: AAOIFI SS 45 §4/2/4's independence test for a third-party capital-protection provider (administrative independence, no direct or indirect ownership relationship above one half) is a fact about two legal entities. ISB-MUDS-09 can only assert that a reference exists. The determination belongs to Shariah Compliance Review and I have not modelled how it is proven.

Pool weightage versus profit-sharing ratio is a jurisdictional fork. Malaysian and Gulf practice both appear in the sources, and whether weightages and a PSR are applied together or as alternatives is an SSB/product decision. Both fields are present and the generated calculation applies weightage then PSR; if a jurisdiction uses only one, the other is 1/1. I could not find a standard that fixes the order, so the order is a declared convention in the catalog, not a cited rule.

balanceBasis DEPOSIT_EQUIVALENT vs UNITISED_INVESTMENT changes what a redemption means (an amount versus a unit valuation), and a unitised account really needs unit and NAV fields. I did not model units: a NAV is a valuation with its own frequency, source and rounding policy, and inventing one would be exactly the manufactured-authority failure this phase forbids. A unitised Mudarabah product cannot be served correctly from this catalog entry as it stands.

No dormancy, no minimum balance, no tiering. BNM ¶25.2 requires eligibility criteria for profit distribution to be disclosed, but no source in the research set fixes them, so no thresholds are in the catalog.

Zakat is referenced from the disclosure BQ only (CUSTOMER_OBLIGATION_INFORMATIONAL / BANK_PAYS_ON_BEHALF). The calculation belongs to the Zakat Calculation domain in the governance area, and the nisab/hawl parameters there are genuinely contested (silver 595 g per AAOIFI SS 35 p.874 versus gold at 85 g or 87.48 g); it is not my area and I have not modelled it.
