RESTRICTED investment accounts are modelled only as mandate ROWS. Whether the mandate is actually honoured is a question about the asset side — the pool's holdings — which lives in the treasury and financing areas, not here. A generated mandate-breach check would be a facade; I have not written one and the gap is real: this catalog can record a restriction and cannot enforce it.

AAOIFI FAS 47 (Transfer of Assets between Investment Pools) governs pool-boundary integrity, which matters when a term account's funds move between pools at rollover. I have not modelled pool transfer: it needs a pool-side control record that belongs to the Profit Calculation And Distribution domain, and I did not want to invent a cross-domain posting shape that the owner of that pool model should define.

profitPayoutFrequency MONTHLY/QUARTERLY on a term account looks, from the outside, exactly like an interest coupon. It is modelled because interim on-account distribution is explicitly permitted by AAOIFI SS 13 §8/8, but a payout schedule plus a stable declared rate is precisely the pattern AAOIFI SS 19 §4/1 calls 'customary practice'. This is a presentation risk the data model cannot resolve and an SSB must look at.

No mention of a Tawarruq-based term deposit. The organised-tawarruq construct that many banks use for term deposits is a different contract chain and would be a different domain entry (Commodity Murabaha Tawarruq exists in the Islamic Financing area); I did not stretch this entry to cover it.

serviceDomains.name: Wakala Investment Account

fields.name: customerReference
fields.note: the principal (muwakkil). The institution is the agent (wakil).

fields.name: lossBearer
fields.note: the principal bears investment loss; the agent is liable only for wilful misconduct, negligence or breach (AAOIFI SS 46 §7/1).

fields.name: agencyFeeBasis
fields.note: AAOIFI SS 46 §5/1 — the agency fee must be a fixed amount or a percentage of the amount INVESTED. Never a percentage of profit: that would make the wakil a partner.

fields.name: expectedProfitRate
fields.note: the Wakala-specific field. AAOIFI SS 46 §6/5 — the profit in its entirety is the principal's unless an excess above the EXPECTED profit is stipulated as the agent's performance incentive. It is an anticipation, never a promise.

fields.name: performanceIncentiveShare
fields.note: the agent's share OF THE EXCESS above expectedProfitRate only

fields.name: perReference
fields.note: AAOIFI SS 46 §6/6–6/7 — the agent may retain a profit-equalisation reserve FOR THE BENEFIT OF THE PRINCIPAL, and on liquidation the balance is returned to the principal. A Wakala PER therefore has no shareholder portion; see PER-07.

fields.name: investedBaseMinor
fields.note: the amount invested that the percentage was applied to; zero for FIXED_AMOUNT

fields.name: expectedProfitMinor
fields.note: ratioMul(investedBaseMinor, expectedProfitRateApplied), truncated toward zero

fields.name: agencyFeeDisclosure
fields.note: BNM PD 028-63 ¶13.1(a)(ii) — for wakalah, the profit after deducting the agency fee and any agreed performance incentive fee must be disclosed.

citation: DESIGN.md §7. AAOIFI SS 45 §3/6 — it is not permissible to stipulate that the investment manager is unconditionally liable for loss of capital
so there is no guaranteed amount to confirm.
AAOIFI SS 46 §6/5 — in a Wakala bi al-istithmar the profit in its entirety belongs to the principal; the agent earns a FEE
plus at most a stipulated share of the excess above expected profit. A profit-sharing ratio on a Wakala record would recharacterise the contract as a Mudarabah.
rules.note: The single most likely generator error in this business area: four of five account domains look alike, and a template that copies the Mudarabah shape onto Wakala produces a contract that does not exist. This lint is why the rule is in the catalog and not in a code review.

citation: AAOIFI SS 46 §5/1 — the fee is a fixed amount OR a percentage of the amount invested. Exactly one
never both
never a share of profit.
rules.note: absent_value() is a runtime null check on a declared field, distinct from absent(), which is the generator-time check that the field is not declared at all.

citation: AAOIFI SS 46 §5/1 — a benchmark-linked fee 'should
however
be capped and floored'.
rules.test: benchmarkLinked=true with cap 500000 and floor 100000 -> accepted; benchmarkLinked=true with cap null -> rejected; cap 100000 and floor 500000 -> rejected.

rules.assert: bq.fee_charge.basisApplied == 'PERCENT_OF_INVESTED' -> bq.fee_charge.amountMinor == ratioMul(bq.fee_charge.investedBaseMinor, bq.fee_charge.rateApplied) || bq.fee_charge.capApplied || bq.fee_charge.floorApplied
citation: AAOIFI SS 46 §5/1 — the fee is a percentage of the amount invested
so the charged amount must be reproducible from the invested base and the rate. A cap or floor is the only permitted divergence and must be flagged on the row.
rules.test: investedBase 10000000, rate 75/10000 -> 75000 exactly (10000000*75/10000). investedBase 10000001, rate 75/10000 -> 75000 (truncated toward zero, remainder 75 discarded); the generated test asserts truncation, not rounding, so the behaviour is pinned.

rules.assert: bq.incentive.excessAboveExpectedMinor == max(0, bq.incentive.realisedProfitMinor - bq.incentive.expectedProfitMinor) && bq.incentive.incentiveAmountMinor == ratioMul(bq.incentive.excessAboveExpectedMinor, bq.incentive.incentiveShareApplied) && (performanceIncentiveApplies == true || bq.incentive.incentiveAmountMinor == 0)
citation: AAOIFI SS 46 §6/5 — the agent may be entitled to all or part of any EXCESS ABOVE THE EXPECTED PROFIT as a performance incentive in addition to its fixed fee. Nothing below the expected profit is the agent's.
rules.test: expected 100000, realised 90000 -> excess 0 and incentive 0 (a shortfall never produces an incentive, and never a clawback from the principal's profit). expected 100000, realised 130000, share 20/100 -> excess 30000, incentive 6000.

rules.assert: balanceMinor >= 0 && balanceMinor == contributedCapitalMinor - redeemedCapitalMinor + cumulativeProfitCreditedMinor - cumulativeCapitalLossBorneMinor - cumulativeAgencyFeeChargedMinor - cumulativePerformanceIncentiveMinor
citation: AAOIFI SS 45 §4/1/1 — loss is borne according to the share in capital
bounded by the capital. The fee and the incentive are deducted from the principal's position
so they belong in the identity.
rules.test: contributed 10000000, profit 250000, fee 75000, incentive 6000, loss 0 -> balance 10169000. Any other value is rejected by the CHECK.

citation: AAOIFI SS 47 §7/2 (neither capital nor profit may be guaranteed); BNM PD 028-63 ¶24.5.
BNM PD 028-63 ¶13.1(a)(ii) and ¶25.2; AAOIFI SS 38 §5/4/1; IFSB-31 Principle 9.
AAOIFI SS 46 §7/1 — the agent is liable for breach of contract
which presupposes a recorded mandate to breach.

shariah.capitalAtRiskNote: Hard true. The agent invests on the principal's behalf and is not liable for loss other than wilful misconduct, negligence or breach (AAOIFI SS 46 §7/1).
shariah.profitSharing: NONE — a Wakala has no profit-sharing ratio. The agent takes a fee and, at most, a share of the excess above the expected profit.
shariah.review: UNREVIEWED — requires named Shariah board sign-off
standards: AAOIFI SS 46 (Al-Wakalah Bi Al-Istithmar) §5/1 — agency fee is a fixed amount or a percentage of the amount invested; a benchmark-linked fee must be capped and floored.

AAOIFI SS 46 §6/5 — the profit in its entirety is the principal's unless the agent is stipulated a share of the excess above the expected profit as a performance incentive in addition to its fixed fee.
AAOIFI SS 46 §6/6–6/7 — the agent may retain a profit-equalisation reserve for the benefit of the principal; on liquidation the balance is returned to the principal.
AAOIFI SS 46 §7/1 — the agent is not liable for loss other than wilful misconduct, negligence or breach of contract.
AAOIFI SS 45 §3/4, §3/6 — manager liability limits; unconditional liability for capital loss may not be stipulated.
AAOIFI SS 47 §7/2, §9 — expected rate without guarantee; mandatory disclosure of the profit-calculation method.
AAOIFI FAS 45 — investment accounts are quasi-equity.

BNM PD 028-63 ¶13.1(a)(ii), ¶13.4, ¶24.5, ¶25.2(b)(iii), ¶27.6 — wakalah profit after agency fee and performance incentive; fee setting inputs; terminology prohibition; disclosure of the fee with clear illustrations; disclosure of average agency and performance incentive fees by tenure and type.

uncertain: AAOIFI SS 46 §6/6 permits a Wakala PER for the principal's benefit, returned on liquidation. IFSB GN-3's PER, by contrast, is shared between IAH and shareholders. These are not the same instrument under the same name. I have modelled the Profit Equalization Reserve domain on the IFSB GN-3 shape and added PER-07 to force a Wakala-linked reserve to have a zero shareholder portion, but whether one reserve record can honestly serve both contracts is a question for the SSB, and I would not be surprised to be told they need separate control records.

Whether a Wakala account participates in a commingled pool at all, or holds identified assets, is a product decision I could not resolve from the sources. poolReference is required because the master catalog's use case is explicitly 'attribute investment-account balances to profit-sharing pools'; an asset-identified Wakala would need a holdings structure this entry does not have.

The agency fee is modelled as charged from the principal's position (it reduces balanceMinor). Charging the fee out of the pool before attribution would produce a different and also defensible model. No source in the research set settles it, and the two differ in what the customer sees, so this is a declared convention, not a cited rule.

AAOIFI SS 46 §5/1 says the fee may be benchmark-linked. A benchmark is an external rate feed with a source, an asOf and a fallback when the publication is missing. I have not modelled the feed; a benchmark-linked fee cannot be computed from this catalog entry alone.

serviceDomains.name: Profit Calculation And Distribution

fields.name: poolReference
fields.note: self-referential by design: the pool is this domain's own aggregate. See `uncertain` — the pool control record itself is NOT modelled here.

fields.name: poolContractType
fields.note: a distribution run operates on a pool whose contract type determines the waterfall: a Mudarabah pool deducts a mudarib share, a Wakala pool deducts an agency fee and at most an incentive. PCD-09 forbids mixing them.

fields.name: currency
fields.note: one run, one currency. A multi-currency pool is multiple runs; converting inside the waterfall would put a rate inside a profit calculation.

fields.name: runType
fields.note: SIMULATION satisfies the master catalog's 're-run hypothetical scenarios before changing weightings' use case. PCD-08 forbids a SIMULATION run from ever posting.

fields.name: supersedesRunRef
fields.note: a FINAL run supersedes a PROVISIONAL one by reference, through a REVERSAL. AAOIFI SS 13 §8/8: two postings, never an update in place.

fields.name: poolCapitalIntact
fields.note: AAOIFI SS 13 §8/7 — no profit may be recognised or claimed unless the capital of the Mudarabah is maintained intact. Stored on the run, not computed at read time, so the determination that licensed a distribution is auditable afterwards.

fields.name: grossPoolIncomeMinor
fields.note: signed: a pool can have a loss-making period

fields.name: perAppropriationMinor
fields.note: step 1 of the waterfall, BEFORE the mudarib share (IFSB GN-3 ¶20)

fields.name: perUtilisedForSmoothingMinor
fields.note: a drawdown of PER to smooth this period's payout. Never to cover a capital loss (IFSB-30 ¶256).

fields.name: mudaribShareMinor
fields.note: step 2. May be waived downward; may never exceed the contractual ceiling (IFSB GN-3 fn.13). Zero when poolContractType is Wakala.

fields.name: mudaribShareCeilingMinor
fields.note: ratioMul(profitAfterPer, contractualMaximumMudaribShare), stored so the waiver is visible as the gap between ceiling and actual

fields.name: agencyFeeMinor
fields.note: the Wakala analogue of the mudarib share. Zero when poolContractType is Mudarabah.

fields.name: irrAppropriationMinor
fields.note: step 3, AFTER the mudarib share, out of the profit attributable to IAH (IFSB GN-3 ¶25)

fields.name: irrUtilisedForLossMinor
fields.note: IRR drawn down to cover a loss on IAH investments — the only permitted use (IFSB GN-3 ¶20; IFSB-30 ¶256)

fields.name: roundingResidualMinor
fields.note: THE one rounding point in this business area: an int64 distributable profit cannot always be split exactly across N accounts. The residual is stored, bounded by PCD-04, and disposed of per roundingPolicy. It is never silently absorbed into the bank's share.

fields.name: roundingPolicy
fields.note: an SSB and jurisdiction choice, not a developer default. Both options keep the residual inside the IAH side; a third option that routes it to the bank is deliberately NOT offered, because that would be an unagreed increase in the mudarib's share.

fields.name: lossCarriedForwardMinor
fields.note: AAOIFI SS 13 §8/7 — losses are carried forward and set against future profits

fields.name: lossBorneByInstitutionMinor
fields.note: non-zero ONLY where the SSB has determined misconduct, negligence or breach. See PCD-06.

fields.name: smoothingJurisdictionPermitted
fields.note: BNM PD 028-63 ¶13.5 forbids profit smoothing and displaced-commercial-risk techniques outright, while AAOIFI SS 46 §6/6 and IFSB GN-3 permit PER/IRR. Smoothing is therefore a jurisdiction-configurable capability and must never be a hard-coded behaviour.

behaviourQualifiers.name: Pool Income Allocation

fields.name: shariahNonCompliantIncomeMinor
fields.note: quarantined: must be excluded from distributable profit and routed to Income Purification. Never distributed to IAH, never into P&L.

behaviourQualifiers.note: IFSB-22 Template 11 and Template 12 require quantitative disclosure by CONTRACT TYPE and by ECONOMIC ACTIVITY. Both are rows here, so the regulatory report is a projection of the run rather than a separate spreadsheet.

fields.name: psrApplied
fields.note: null for a Wakala account: there is no profit-sharing ratio

behaviourQualifiers.name: Calculation Lineage

fields.name: sequence
fields.note: the normative waterfall order (IFSB GN-3 ¶20/¶25). A row out of sequence is a rule violation, not a display problem.

fields.name: truncatedRemainderMinor
fields.note: whatever ratioMul discarded at this step. Recording it is what makes 'no float' an auditable claim rather than a slogan.

behaviourQualifiers.note: append-only. The master catalog's use case is 'publish calculation lineage for SSB review and customer queries'; DESIGN.md §5.8 requires append-only audit for every Shariah finding. Every input that moved a money field is a row, so the run is replayable.

rules.assert: iahDistributableProfitMinor == grossPoolIncomeMinor - allocatedExpensesMinor - sum(bq.income_source.shariahNonCompliantIncomeMinor) - perAppropriationMinor + perUtilisedForSmoothingMinor - mudaribShareMinor - agencyFeeMinor - irrAppropriationMinor + irrUtilisedForLossMinor
citation: IFSB GN-3 ¶20 and ¶25 — PER is appropriated out of pool profit BEFORE the allocation to shareholders and UIAH and before the mudarib share is calculated; IRR is set aside out of the profit attributable to IAH AFTER deducting the mudarib share. AAOIFI SS 13 §9/6 and the SNC treatment keep non-compliant income out of distributable profit.
rules.note: The single most valuable generated test in this business area. Exact int64 equality — no tolerance, no epsilon, no rounding slack. The waterfall ORDER is not merely a convention: PER before the mudarib share makes the bank share in the smoothing, IRR after it does not.
rules.test: gross 100000000, expenses 5000000, snc 0, perAppropriation 2000000, perUtilised 0, mudaribShare 18600000, agencyFee 0, irrAppropriation 1000000, irrUtilised 0 -> iahDistributable 73400000. Change any single input by 1 minor unit and the assertion must fail.

rules.assert: mudaribShareMinor <= mudaribShareCeilingMinor && mudaribShareCeilingMinor == ratioMul(grossPoolIncomeMinor - allocatedExpensesMinor - perAppropriationMinor + perUtilisedForSmoothingMinor, contractualMaximumMudaribShare)
citation: IFSB GN-3 fn.13 — no unilateral increase of the mudarib share above the contractual maximum. The share may be waived DOWNWARD
which is why the assertion is <= and the ceiling is stored.
rules.test: profitAfterPer 93000000, contractualMaximumMudaribShare 20/100 -> ceiling 18600000. mudaribShare 18600000 accepted; 18600001 rejected; 0 accepted (full waiver).

citation: AAOIFI SS 13 §8/7 — no profit can be recognised or claimed unless the capital is maintained intact; losses are carried forward and set against future profits. A mudarib share on a loss-making period is a fee on a loss
which the Mudarabah contract does not permit.
rules.note: The agency fee is set to zero here too, which is the STRICTER reading. AAOIFI SS 46 §5/1 makes the Wakala fee a fee on the amount invested, not on profit, so a literal reading would let it stand in a loss period. Flagged in `uncertain`.

citation: UNSOURCED as a Shariah clause; it is the arithmetic consequence of distributing an int64 across N holders without a float. AAOIFI SS 47 §8/2 is the nearest hook: institutions must avoid methods of profit calculation or distribution that are misleading.
rules.note: The bound `roundingResidualMinor < accountCount` is what stops a rounding residual being used as a silent skim: with a correct largest-remainder allocation each account is short by at most one minor unit, so the residual cannot exceed the number of accounts.
rules.test: iahDistributed 1000000, accountCount 3, allocations 333334 + 333333 + 333333 -> residual 0, accepted. allocations 333333 x3 -> residual 1, accepted. allocations 300000 x3 -> residual 100000, rejected (>= accountCount).

citation: BNM PD 028-63 ¶13.5 — 'The IFI must not implement profit smoothing practices or displaced commercial risk (DCR) techniques.' This directly contradicts AAOIFI SS 46 §6/6 and IFSB GN-3
which permit PER/IRR. The contradiction is real and is resolved by configuration with a named authority
never by a default in code.
IFSB GN-3 fn.12 citing IFSB-2 ¶76 — 'the IIFS as Mudarib is not permitted to absorb losses incurred on the IAH's investment as this is not Shari'ah compliant
except in the case of misconduct or negligence'. AAOIFI SS 13 §4/4 and SS 45 §3/4 to the same effect.
rules.note: A commercially tempting kindness — the bank quietly covering a bad month — is a Shariah violation. The code cannot decide that misconduct occurred; it refuses the posting until the Shariah Compliance Review domain has recorded a determination.

citation: AAOIFI SS 13 §8/7 (capital intact); IFSB-30 Principle 18 ¶272 (IAH entitled to the method); DESIGN.md §5.8 (append-only audit). Non-compliant income must be routed to purification before anything is declared.
UNSOURCED as a Shariah clause; it is the containment rule the master catalog's scenario use case requires. A simulation that can post is an unaudited distribution.
AAOIFI SS 13 §8/1 (mudarib takes a share of profit) versus AAOIFI SS 46 §5/1 and §6/5 (the wakil takes a fee on the amount invested plus at most a share of the excess). A pool cannot do both at once
and a run that charged both would be charging twice for one role.
AAOIFI SS 13 §8/8 — an interim distribution on account is revised when actual or constructive valuation takes place. Modelled as two postings; the provisional run is reversed
never edited.
UNSOURCED. A guard against the failure mode no standard names: every ratioMul truncation discards a remainder
and if those remainders are not accounted for
money leaves the waterfall without a destination. FLAG rather than reject
because the bound is heuristic — see `uncertain`.

events.name: profit.loss.carried.forward
events.note: the event with no conventional counterpart: a distribution run that distributes nothing because the pool lost money

events.name: profit.snc.income.quarantined
events.note: consumed by Income Purification and Shariah Compliance Review; append-only

shariah.contractTypeNote: A distribution run is not itself a contract. It operates on a pool whose contract type is per-pool, which is why poolContractType is a stored, queryable field and PCD-09 forbids the two waterfalls being mixed. DESIGN.md §7's ContractType enum has no value for a process domain, so Mudarabah is recorded here as the dominant case.
shariah.capitalAtRiskNote: The funds this run operates on are IAH capital that bears loss. The run can distribute a loss, and a loss-bearing distribution is exactly the thing a conventional interest engine cannot express.
shariah.review: UNREVIEWED — requires named Shariah board sign-off
standards: IFSB GN-3 (Guidance Note on the Practice of Smoothing the Profits Payout to Investment Account Holders, Dec 2010) ¶20, ¶25 — the normative waterfall order: PER before the allocation to shareholders and UIAH and before the mudarib share; IRR after deducting the mudarib share, usable only to cover losses on UIAH investments.
IFSB GN-3 ¶26, ¶27 — PER collectively belongs to IAH and shareholders; IRR is created in the equity of IAH.
IFSB GN-3 ¶28 — IAH agree in advance on the proportion of their income that may be appropriated to each reserve.

IFSB GN-3 fn.12 (citing IFSB-2 ¶76) — the IIFS as mudarib may not absorb IAH investment losses except for misconduct or negligence. fn.13 — no unilateral increase of the mudarib share above the contractual maximum.

AAOIFI SS 13 §8/1, §8/7, §8/8, §9/6 — profit as an agreed percentage; capital intact before recognition; interim distribution revised on actual or constructive valuation; no gift or donation out of Mudarabah funds.
AAOIFI SS 46 §5/1, §6/5 — the Wakala alternative: a fee on the amount invested plus at most a share of the excess above expected profit.
AAOIFI SS 47 §8/2, §9 — no misleading or deceptive methods of profit calculation or distribution; the method must be disclosed and open to client inquiry.
AAOIFI FAS 35 — Risk Reserves, the standard governing PER and IRR. AAOIFI FAS 45 — Quasi-equity (Including Investment Accounts).

IFSB-30 Principle 15 ¶256 — the PER shall not be used to compensate for a loss in capital; the IRR serves that purpose. Principle 18 ¶272, ¶276–¶278 — IAH information rights, PSR in advance, publication of smoothing and of material policy changes.
IFSB-22 Template 10, Template 11, Template 12 — PSIA quantitative disclosures by contract and by economic activity, with the PER split between shareholders and IAH and the IRR balance as line items.
BNM PD 028-63 ¶13.5 — profit smoothing and DCR techniques are forbidden in Malaysia; ¶27.6 — 'declared rate of return' is the correct term for the realised figure.

uncertain: THE BIGGEST GAP IN MY AREA: there is no pool control record. This domain's catalog entry models the RUN, and a run references a pool by string. A pool has its own identity, asset side, opening and closing equity, carried-forward losses, participating accounts and FAS 47 transfer rules. A clean design would make 'Investment Pool' a tenth service domain in this business area — a Maintain or Administer pattern on an 'Investment Pool' asset type — and the master catalog does not have one. I did not add a domain to the catalog because the task says to read the domain list rather than invent it, so I am reporting it instead: the 48-domain decomposition has a hole where the pool should be, and lossCarriedForwardMinor on a run is a per-run number with nowhere authoritative to accumulate.

PCD-03 forces the Wakala agency fee to zero in a loss period. That is my stricter reading, not a cited rule: AAOIFI SS 46 §5/1 makes the fee a charge on the amount invested rather than on profit, so a literal reading would let the fee stand and deepen the IAH's loss. I chose the reading that cannot overcharge a customer and I am flagging it, because an SSB may well say the fee is due regardless.

PCD-11's bound (sum of truncated remainders <= residual + accountCount) is heuristic. I could derive a tight bound only for the final allocation step, not for a chain of ratioMul operations whose remainders partly cancel. It is therefore a FLAG, and the generated test pins current behaviour rather than proving a limit. A tight bound needs the waterfall's step count, which is data the template has.

Expense allocation to the pool (allocatedExpensesMinor) is modelled as one number. Which expenses may be charged to IAH funds at all is a contested Shariah question — AAOIFI SS 19 §9/2 excludes indirect expenses from qard service charges, and BNM ¶27.6 requires allocated expenses to be disclosed as a line item — but no source in the research set gives a closed list for a Mudarabah pool. One opaque number is the honest shape; a breakdown would imply an authority I do not have.

The run is single-currency by construction. A real pool holding assets in several currencies needs a conversion step, and a conversion rate inside a profit waterfall is the single most dangerous place in this design (DESIGN.md §6). I kept it out: multi-currency pools are not servable from this entry.

Pakistan's State Bank caps for these reserves (reportedly IRR <= 10% and PER <= 30% of Islamic Banking Equity, with a minimum 75% of weighted-average gross yield on PKR savings from 1 Jan 2025) appear in the research only via secondary sources. They are NOT in this catalog as numbers. See the reserve domains' jurisdictionCapShare field.

serviceDomains.name: Profit Equalization Reserve

fields.name: iahPortionMinor
fields.note: IFSB GN-3 ¶26 — 'The PER collectively belongs to IAH and shareholders'. The split is the whole reason PER is a different instrument from IRR.

fields.name: appropriationPoint
fields.note: IFSB GN-3 ¶20 — appropriated out of the profits of the commingled pool BEFORE allocation to shareholders and UIAH, and before the mudarib share is calculated. A const because getting this wrong silently changes who pays for the smoothing.

fields.name: useRestrictedTo
fields.note: IFSB-30 ¶256 — 'The PER shall not be used to compensate for the loss in capital, and for this purpose a special type of reserve is used, which is the investment risk reserve.'

fields.name: contractualMaxAppropriationShare
fields.note: IFSB GN-3 ¶28 — IAH agree IN ADVANCE on the proportion of their income that may be appropriated. Per-account/per-pool contractual data, not a policy knob.

fields.name: jurisdictionPermitted
fields.note: BNM PD 028-63 ¶13.5 forbids smoothing and DCR outright; AAOIFI SS 46 §6/6 and IFSB GN-3 permit PER. A false here disables every appropriation and utilisation (PER-05).

fields.name: jurisdictionCapShare
fields.note: a regulator's cap on the reserve balance as a share of a declared base. NULLABLE AND EMPTY BY DEFAULT: the caps reported for Pakistan (PER <= 30% of Islamic Banking Equity) reached the research only through secondary sources, so no number is in this catalog. A value here must arrive as configuration with a cited source.

fields.name: onTerminationIahPortionTreatment
fields.note: IFSB GN-3 ¶28 and IFSB-30 ¶254 — IAH agree to give up rights to the reserves on termination, and exit is based on forgoing their portion in undistributed profits, PER and IRR. AAOIFI SS 46 §6/7 says the opposite for a Wakala PER: on liquidation the balance is RETURNED to the principal. Hence an enum with no default.

fields.name: disclosurePublishedAt
fields.note: IFSB-30 ¶277 — PER utilisation for smoothing 'needs to be publicised'.

fields.name: mechanicsDescription
fields.note: IFSB-30 ¶272 — IAH are entitled to be informed of the 'mechanics of smoothing the returns (if any)'.

rules.assert: balanceMinor == iahPortionMinor + shareholderPortionMinor && balanceMinor >= 0 && iahPortionMinor >= 0 && shareholderPortionMinor >= 0
citation: IFSB GN-3 ¶26 — the PER collectively belongs to IAH and shareholders. Every minor unit of the balance belongs to one of the two.
rules.test: balance 5000000 = iah 4000000 + shareholder 1000000 -> accepted; iah 4000000 + shareholder 999999 -> rejected.

citation: IFSB GN-3 ¶28 — IAH agree in advance on the proportion of their income that may be appropriated to the reserve. More than the agreed proportion is an unagreed withholding of the customer's profit.
rules.test: poolProfitBeforeAppropriation 95000000, contractualMaxAppropriationShare 25/1000 -> maximum 2375000. amount 2000000 accepted; 2375001 rejected.

citation: IFSB-30 Principle 15 ¶256 — 'The PER shall not be used to compensate for the loss in capital
and for this purpose a special type of reserve is used
which is the investment risk reserve.' The enum has exactly one value so that the wrong purpose is unrepresentable
not merely rejected.
UNSOURCED as a clause; a reserve cannot be drawn below zero without becoming a loan from the shareholders to the IAH
which no source in the research set permits.
BNM PD 028-63 ¶13.5 — 'The IFI must not implement profit smoothing practices or displaced commercial risk (DCR) techniques.' PER/IRR is a jurisdictional fork
not a feature: the capability must be switchable off entirely
and in Malaysia it is off.
Jurisdiction-specific and NOT verified in the research (the Pakistan caps came from secondary sources). FLAG
and only when a cap has been configured with a cited source. No cap number is in this catalog.
rules.note: capBaseAmountMinor is supplied by the caller from the IFSB Regulatory Reporting domain; this service does not compute Islamic Banking Equity.

citation: AAOIFI SS 46 §6/6–6/7 — the agent may retain a profit-equalisation reserve FOR THE BENEFIT OF THE PRINCIPAL and 'upon liquidation
the balance of the profit equalisation reserve is returned to the principal'. That is not IFSB GN-3's shared PER. Keeping both under one control record requires this rule; see `uncertain`.
IFSB-30 Principle 18 ¶277 — PER utilisation for smoothing and IRR use for covering losses 'needs to be publicised'. FLAG rather than reject: the publication is an act outside this service
so the service records that it is owed.

shariah.contractTypeNote: A reserve is not a contract. It belongs to a pool and takes the pool's contract type, which is why poolContractType is stored and PER-07 exists. DESIGN.md §7's enum has no value for a reserve.
shariah.capitalAtRiskNote: The reserve is funded out of IAH profit and partly belongs to IAH, so it sits on the at-risk side of the balance sheet. It is explicitly NOT a capital guarantee: IFSB-30 ¶256 forbids using it to compensate a capital loss.
shariah.permittedUnder: AAOIFI and IFSB permit PER. Bank Negara Malaysia forbids it (BNM PD 028-63 ¶13.5). This domain is therefore jurisdiction-gated by a stored flag, not by a build-time choice.
shariah.review: UNREVIEWED — requires named Shariah board sign-off
standards: IFSB GN-3 ¶20 — PER is appropriated out of the profits of the commingled pool before the allocation to shareholders and UIAH and before the mudarib share is calculated.
IFSB GN-3 ¶26 — the PER collectively belongs to IAH and shareholders.
IFSB GN-3 ¶28 — IAH agree in advance on the proportion of their income appropriated to each reserve, and agree to give up rights to those reserves on termination.
IFSB-30 Principle 15 ¶256 — the PER shall not be used to compensate for a loss in capital. ¶254 — IAH exit is based on forgoing their portion in undistributed profits, PER and IRR.
IFSB-30 Principle 18 ¶272, ¶277, ¶278 — the mechanics of smoothing must be disclosed; PER utilisation needs to be publicised; material changes to smoothing policy require timely public announcement.
IFSB-22 Template 12 — the PER split between shareholders and IAH as a reported line item.
AAOIFI FAS 35 — Risk Reserves: the AAOIFI financial-accounting standard governing PER and IRR (with FAS 30, superseding FAS 11).
AAOIFI SS 46 §6/6–6/7 — the Wakala variant: a PER retained for the principal's benefit and returned to the principal on liquidation.
BNM PD 028-63 ¶13.5 — profit smoothing and DCR techniques are forbidden in Malaysia.

uncertain: AAOIFI SS 46 §6/6-6/7's Wakala PER and IFSB GN-3's shared PER are arguably two different instruments wearing one name: the Wakala reserve belongs wholly to the principal and is returned on liquidation, while the GN-3 reserve is shared with shareholders and forgone on exit. I modelled one control record with poolContractType plus PER-07 rather than two domains, because the catalog has one Profit Equalization Reserve domain. An SSB may split them, and that would be a new catalog entry, not a code change.

Whether the IAH's PER portion is forgone or returned on termination is contract terms, and the two cited sources point opposite ways (IFSB GN-3 ¶28 / IFSB-30 ¶254 versus AAOIFI SS 46 §6/7). onTerminationIahPortionTreatment therefore has no default. A generator that defaults it would be choosing a Shariah position.

The iah/shareholder split RATIO on each appropriation is not modelled. I store the two amounts per row and assert they sum, but what determines the split is not in the sources I have — it may follow the PSR, the pool's equity proportions, or a separate contractual term. Storing a ratio I cannot cite would be inventing one.

jurisdictionCapShare is deliberately empty. The Pakistan caps (PER <= 30% of Islamic Banking Equity, IRR <= 10%) appear in the research only through secondary sources, and the cap base, Islamic Banking Equity, is computed in the IFSB Regulatory Reporting domain, not here. PER-06 flags rather than rejects, and only when a cap has been configured with a cited source.

A smoothed payout is, economically, closer to a fixed return than an unsmoothed one. Whether a given smoothing practice crosses from permitted equalisation into an implied guarantee is a judgement that no field can hold. The model records the mechanics so the SSB can see them; it cannot decide them.

serviceDomains.name: Investment Risk Reserve

fields.name: poolContractType
fields.note: IFSB GN-3 ¶25 defines IRR by reference to the mudarib share. No source in the research set describes an IRR for a Wakala pool, so the enum has one value rather than a guess.

fields.name: equityOwner
fields.note: IFSB GN-3 ¶27 — the IRR 'is created in the equity of IAH'. Unlike the PER there is NO shareholder portion, which is why no such field exists on this record (IRR-05).

fields.name: appropriationPoint
fields.note: IFSB GN-3 ¶25 — set aside out of the profit attributable to IAH, AFTER deducting the IIFS's mudarib share. The contrast with the PER's BEFORE is the whole substance of the distinction between the two reserves.

fields.name: useRestrictedTo
fields.note: IFSB GN-3 ¶20 — 'can be used only to cover losses on the investments of UIAH funds'. IFSB-30 ¶256 makes the IRR, not the PER, the reserve for capital loss.

fields.name: jurisdictionCapShare
fields.note: empty by default, for the same reason as the PER's: the reported Pakistan cap (IRR <= 10%) is from secondary sources only.

fields.name: iahProfitAfterMudaribShareMinor
fields.note: the base. Named at length on purpose: appropriating from the wrong base is the error this reserve is most prone to.

citation: UNSOURCED as a clause; the reserve is an accumulation and must reconcile to its own movements.
rules.test: appropriated 3000000, utilised 1200000 -> balance 1800000 accepted; balance 1800001 rejected.

citation: IFSB GN-3 ¶25 — the IRR is set aside 'out of the profit attributable to IAH
after deducting the IIFS's Mudarib share'. Appropriating before the mudarib share would make the shareholders co-fund a reserve that belongs wholly to IAH
which is the PER's job
not the IRR's. IFSB GN-3 ¶28 bounds the share.
rules.test: iahProfitAfterMudaribShare 74400000, contractualMaxAppropriationShare 15/1000 -> maximum 1116000. amount 1000000 accepted; 1116001 rejected. The base must equal the run's post-mudarib figure exactly, not the pre-mudarib one.

citation: IFSB GN-3 ¶20 — the IRR can be used ONLY to cover losses on the investments of UIAH funds. IFSB-30 ¶256 confirms it is the reserve for capital loss. A drawdown larger than the loss would be a distribution
and larger than the balance would be a loan.
BNM PD 028-63 ¶13.5 — profit smoothing and DCR techniques are forbidden in Malaysia
and the IRR is part of that practice. The capability must be switchable off entirely.
IFSB GN-3 ¶27 — the IRR 'is created in the equity of IAH'
in contrast to ¶26's PER which 'collectively belongs to IAH and shareholders'. A shareholder-portion field on an IRR record would be a category error
so it must be impossible to express rather than merely set to zero. This is the structural difference between the two reserve domains
and a generator that produced them from one shared shape would erase it.
Jurisdiction-specific and NOT verified. No cap number is in this catalog.
IFSB-30 Principle 18 ¶277 — IRR use for covering losses needs to be publicised.

events.name: irr.utilised
events.note: this event means IAH capital was about to be reduced and the reserve absorbed it. It is the one event in the business area that should always reach the regulator's report.

shariah.capitalAtRiskNote: The IRR exists BECAUSE capital is at risk: it is the reserve that absorbs an IAH investment loss. It does not make the capital guaranteed — it is funded from IAH's own profit and is created in IAH equity.
shariah.permittedUnder: AAOIFI FAS 35 and IFSB GN-3 permit the IRR. Bank Negara Malaysia forbids the practice (BNM PD 028-63 ¶13.5). Jurisdiction-gated by a stored flag.
shariah.review: UNREVIEWED — requires named Shariah board sign-off
standards: IFSB GN-3 ¶20 — the IRR can be used only to cover losses on the investments of UIAH funds.
IFSB GN-3 ¶25 — the IRR is set aside out of the profit attributable to IAH, after deducting the IIFS's mudarib share.
IFSB GN-3 ¶27 — the IRR is created in the equity of IAH.
IFSB GN-3 ¶28 — IAH agree in advance on the proportion of their income appropriated to each reserve.
IFSB-30 Principle 15 ¶254, ¶256 — the IRR, not the PER, is the reserve for capital loss; IAH exit is based on forgoing their portion in undistributed profits, PER and IRR.
IFSB-30 Principle 18 ¶277 — IRR use for covering losses needs to be publicised.
IFSB-22 Template 12 — IRR balances as a reported line item.
AAOIFI FAS 35 — Risk Reserves: the standard governing PER and IRR.
BNM PD 028-63 ¶13.5 — the practice is forbidden in Malaysia.

uncertain: No source in the research set describes an IRR for a Wakala pool, so poolContractType is pinned to Mudarabah. If a Wakala pool needs one, that is a new fact and a catalog change, not an inference I am entitled to make.

The relationship between the IRR and the account-level cumulativeCapitalLossBorneMinor is not modelled end to end. When the IRR absorbs a loss, the accounts should see a smaller loss attribution; I assert the reserve-side arithmetic and the account-side arithmetic separately and do not assert that they agree. The cross-domain reconciliation needs the pool control record that does not exist (see the Profit Calculation domain's first `uncertain` item), and asserting it from here would be a facade.
Whether the IAH's IRR portion is forgone or returned on termination has the same open question as the PER's, and the field has no default for the same reason.
jurisdictionCapShare is empty by design. The reported Pakistan cap (IRR <= 10%) is secondary-source only in this research, and the cap base is computed elsewhere.

serviceDomains.name: Hibah Discretionary Gift

fields.name: targetContractType
fields.note: a Hibah may only go to a non-capital-at-risk deposit. Paying a 'gift' to a Mudarabah or Wakala investment-account holder would be a return outside the agreed profit mechanism, i.e. a disguised guarantee. Enforced by HIB-02.

fields.name: discretionBasis
fields.note: AAOIFI SS 19 §5/2 — an UNSTIPULATED excess at repayment is permissible. The permission rests entirely on the award being unstipulated, so the only permitted basis is the institution's own discretion.

fields.name: contractuallyStipulated
fields.note: pinned false with a single-value CHECK. AAOIFI SS 19 §4/1 — a stipulated excess is riba whether stipulated in writing or by customary practice. A true here is not a bad record, it is a prohibited product.

fields.name: fundingSource
fields.note: AAOIFI SS 13 §9/6 — the mudarib may not make a loan, gift or charitable donation out of Mudarabah funds. A Hibah funded from the IAH pool would take investment-account holders' money to pay depositors.

fields.name: approvalAuthorityRef
fields.note: the internal body that exercised the discretion, recorded per award

fields.name: cadenceReviewFlag
fields.note: set by HIB-06 when this account's award history starts to look like a customary entitlement. A flag for the Shariah compliance function, never a block on the payment.

behaviourQualifiers.name: Award Decision
behaviourQualifiers.note: append-only decision trail: who exercised the discretion, on what date, with what SSB reference. The discretion is the Shariah basis for the award, so it must be evidenced per award and not per product.

behaviourQualifiers.name: Cadence Observation

fields.name: impliedEffectiveRate
fields.note: computed FOR REVIEW ONLY and never shown to the customer or used to size a future award: doing either would convert the gift into the rate the prohibition is about.

fields.name: thresholdPeriodsConfigured
fields.note: SSB configuration. There is no default in this catalog, because a threshold is a Shariah judgement about when practice becomes custom.

behaviourQualifiers.note: the detection surface for HIB-06. Stored rather than computed on the fly so that a referral to the SSB carries the evidence that triggered it.

rules.assert: contractuallyStipulated == false && derivedFromRate == false && derivedFromSchedule == false && discretionBasis == 'INSTITUTION_DISCRETION_UNSTIPULATED'
citation: AAOIFI SS 19 §4/1 — stipulation of any excess for the lender is riba
'whether the excess is stipulated at the time of the contract or while determining the period of delay ... and
further
whether the stipulation is in writing or is part of customary practice'. AAOIFI SS 19 §5/2 — an unstipulated excess at repayment is permissible
which is the only ground this whole domain stands on.
rules.note: Three single-value CHECK constraints. A stipulated Hibah is not a validation error to be reported to a user; it is a product the database must be unable to hold.

citation: Derived from AAOIFI SS 13 §8/1 and §8/5 (an investment-account holder's return must come from the agreed share of profit

and a stipulated lump sum voids the Mudarabah) together with BNM PD 028-63 ¶24.5 (nothing may represent an investment account as guaranteed). A discretionary gift to an IAH is a return outside the agreed mechanism and reads as a top-up guarantee.
rules.note: Marked derived, not cited: I did not find a clause that says in terms 'no hibah to an investment account'. I believe the inference is sound and I am flagging that it IS an inference.

citation: AAOIFI SS 13 §9/6 — the mudarib may not make a loan
gift or charitable donation out of Mudarabah funds. Funding a depositor's gift from the investment pool spends the IAH's money on someone else's benefit.

rules.assert: absent(hibahRate) && absent(profitRate) && absent(interestRate) && absent(awardSchedule) && absent(declaredRateOfReturn) && absent(guaranteedAmountMinor) && absent(expectedHibahMinor)
citation: AAOIFI SS 19 §4/1 as above; BNM PD 028-63 ¶24.5 — terminology itself can breach.
rules.note: The reason this domain's catalog entry carries no rate field of any kind: a rate the code can store is a rate the product can promise. impliedEffectiveRate exists ONLY on the Cadence Observation behaviour qualifier, as review evidence, and HIB-06 is what keeps it there.

rules.assert: status == 'PAID' -> (exists(approvedAt) && count(bq.decision where decisionType == 'APPROVED') >= 1 && exists(ssbApprovalRef) && count(bq.posting) >= 1)
citation: AAOIFI SS 19 §5/2 — the permission rests on the award being a genuine exercise of discretion
so the discretion must be evidenced per award. AAOIFI SS 19 §9/1 to the same effect for the method being laid down by the Supervisory Board in detail.

AAOIFI SS 19 §4/1 — the prohibition explicitly reaches a stipulation that 'is part of customary practice'. This is the one Shariah risk in this domain that is not a field at all but a PATTERN over time: a gift paid every month at a stable effective rate has become an expectation
and no single award record is wrong.
rules.note: FLAG, and deliberately so. The code raises a Shariah Compliance Review case with the cadence evidence attached; it must not block the payment, because whether custom has formed is a judgement for the SSB and not for a threshold. The threshold itself is configuration with no default in this catalog — see `uncertain`.

citation: DESIGN.md §5.8 — append-only audit. A reversal is a compensating posting
never a deleted row: the award happened and the record of it must survive.

events.name: hibah.award.paid
events.note: consumed by the Wadiah and Qard Hassan account domains as a HIBAH_CREDIT accounting entry, and by AAOIFI Financial Accounting

events.name: hibah.cadence.referred
events.note: goes to Shariah Compliance Review, never to a customer-facing channel: the implied rate is review evidence, and publishing it would create the expectation the rule exists to detect

shariah.contractTypeNote: A Hibah is not itself one of DESIGN.md §7's contract types; it is a gratuitous transfer onto an account whose contract is Qard Hassan or Wadiah. targetContractType carries the real answer per award.
shariah.capitalAtRiskNote: False, and necessarily so: HIB-02 forbids a Hibah to a capital-at-risk account.
shariah.review: UNREVIEWED — requires named Shariah board sign-off
standards: AAOIFI SS 19 (Loan/Qard) §5/2 — an unstipulated excess at repayment is permissible. This is the entire Shariah basis for the domain.
AAOIFI SS 19 §4/1 — a stipulated excess is riba, including where the stipulation is in writing OR is part of customary practice.
AAOIFI SS 19 §10/1/1 — a current account is a loan to the institution, which is why an excess paid on it is governed by the qard rules at all.
AAOIFI SS 19 §9/1 — the method must be laid down by the Supervisory Board of the institution in detail.
AAOIFI SS 13 §9/6 — the mudarib may not make a loan, gift or charitable donation out of Mudarabah funds.
BNM PD 028-63 ¶24.5 — nothing may represent a product as principal or profit guaranteed or equivalent to a deposit.

uncertain: THE HARDEST THING IN MY AREA, and I want to be plain about it: this domain is Shariah-compliant only as long as nobody relies on it. Every individual award can be unstipulated, discretionary and properly approved, and the product can still drift into a customary entitlement, which AAOIFI SS 19 §4/1 catches in terms. HIB-06 detects the drift and refers it; it cannot decide it, and I have deliberately not given thresholdPeriodsConfigured a default. A generator that shipped a default here would be making a Shariah ruling in a config file.

HIB-02 (no Hibah to a capital-at-risk account) is DERIVED, not cited. I did not find a clause stating it directly. It follows from AAOIFI SS 13 §8/1 and §8/5 and BNM ¶24.5, and I think it is right, but an SSB might permit a hibah to an IAH in specific circumstances and then this rule is wrong.

impliedEffectiveRate is computed on the review surface and I am uneasy about it existing at all. The argument for it: a referral without evidence is not actionable. The argument against: the number is one `GET` away from a customer-facing channel, and once a customer sees it the gift has become a rate. The compromise is that it lives only on the Cadence Observation behaviour qualifier and only the referral event carries it, to Shariah Compliance Review. If the openbank-islamic sibling ever exposes it on a customer path, that is a defect and the generated authorization deny-test should say so.

Hibah on a Wadiah account is included because the master catalog places this domain alongside the Wadiah and Qard Hassan products, but under AAOIFI SS 19 §10/1/1 a usable Wadiah balance IS a qard, so the Wadiah case may be the Qard case wearing a different name. Same open question as the two account domains.

Nothing here models tax or withholding on a gift, and nothing models a Hibah in kind (a non-cash gift). Both exist in practice. amountMinor plus a currency cannot express a gift of goods, and I did not invent a shape for one.

rules.note: cost-plus must add up. The derived column makes this structurally true; the rule makes a client that posts its own sellingPriceMinor fail loudly instead of silently.
THE structural-integrity rule: the bank cannot sell what it does not own, and a zero-length ownership window is the commonest real defect. Strict < , not <=.
undisclosed cost makes it a Musawamah sale, not a Murabaha
the schedule may not total anything other than the fixed price
a price that moves after signing is interest wearing a sale's clothes. This is the rule that distinguishes the two.
no late-payment amount reaches income from this domain. The ledger-level proof is ISB-LPC-03 in Late Payment Charity Handling.
flag not reject: a genuine reimbursement of a customer who paid the supplier first exists, but it must be reviewed every time.
a pre-agreed rebate formula reintroduces the time value of money; permitted by some regulators (BNM) and not by others
the wa'd must be a separate instrument; two contracts in one is the defect
a build-time schema assertion. A Murabaha has an amount, never a rate. This one line is what stops the 49th domain reintroducing interest by a new name.

ISB-MRB-02 enforces that the window is non-empty; it cannot assert that the risk was economically real.

including on a LOSS: if netProceeds are below the capital contributed, the shortfall still splits by share

fields.note: The single most load-bearing field in this business area. AssetBacked = legal true sale, certificate holders have recourse to the asset. AssetBased = beneficial ownership only, recourse to the obligor. AAOIFI Shari'ah Standard 62 (Sukuk) — an EXPOSURE DRAFT as of Nov 2026, research-confirmed — is understood to push toward real ownership transfer, so this field is deliberately explicit rather than inferred, to absorb a later requirement without a migration of meaning.

fields.name: debtBasedUnderlying

fields.note: The manager's/mudarib's share of PROFIT as an exact numerator/denominator. The certificate holders' share is the complement (denominator - numerator)/denominator, so the two shares sum to 1 by construction rather than by a validation that can be skipped. It is a share of profit and never a percentage of the certificate's face value — the research cites SS 13 §8/1 for that distinction.

fields.name: contractualMaxMudaribRatio

uncertain: The sukuk standard inside the published AAOIFI set (commonly referenced as SS 17 'Investment Sukuk') was not retrieved by this research, so no clause of it is cited anywhere in this entry. Every sukuk rule here is either an arithmetic identity, an evidence-for-a-claim invariant, or a flag.

Asset-cover ratio: no standard in this research states a required ratio of underlying asset value to issue size. ISB-SUK-ISS-06 therefore asserts only >= 1.0 and flags; the real ratio is SSB/jurisdiction configuration and should become a threshold field once an authority is named.

Tranching / multi-class sukuk and subordination are not modelled. A senior/subordinated split raises a prior question (whether unequal rights over the same undivided asset are permissible) that this agent cannot answer.

Periodic distribution for IjaraRental is modelled as a schedule of amounts, not as a rental formula with a reset. A floating Ijara rental reset against a conventional benchmark is extremely common and contested; it is carried only as expectedPeriodicDistributionBps plus distributionIsIndicative, which is weaker than reality.
SPV/trustee structure is one string field (spvLegalName). A real program has a trust deed, a declaration of trust and a trustee party with duties. That is a separate service domain, not a field.
serviceDomains.summary: Structures and issues a sukuk program. The whole design turns on one distinction the master catalog's own use cases demand and a bond model cannot carry: AssetBacked (true sale, holders own the asset) versus AssetBased (beneficial interest only, recourse to the obligor). Everything else — the structure enum, the underlying-asset pool with per-asset ownership transfer, the no-principal-guarantee invariant, the face-value purchase-undertaking flag — exists to make that distinction evidenced rather than asserted.

uncertain: AGGREGATE CONCENTRATION CANNOT BE EXPRESSED. A per-record rule grammar has no group-by, so 'no single issuer above N bps' is not assertable as a rule over this control record. Rather than inventing a groupSum operator for one case, concentration is computed by a read projection and RECORDED in limitBreaches, and the rules guard that ledger (ISB-SUK-PRT-02/03). If aggregate limits must be enforced at write time, the catalog needs a first-class `aggregates` block and the template a query generator — that is a schema decision for the catalog owner, not something to smuggle in as a free-text assert.

MANDATE CONFORMANCE IS NOT ASSERTED AND NO PLACEHOLDER RULE PRETENDS IT IS. 'Every position's structure must be in permittedStructures' is a join between two sibling arrays, which the grammar cannot express. A rule for it was drafted and then REMOVED, because an assert that does not parse under this fragment's own grammar is a build failure rather than a visible gap, and a rule that silently checks something weaker is worse than an honest absence. The check belongs in the mandate projection alongside concentration.

PER and IRR are NOT modelled here even though a Mudarabah-managed portfolio feeding an investment pool is exactly where smoothing is applied. They belong to isb-profit-equalization-reserve and isb-investment-risk-reserve in the Deposits area. The ordering is normative (PER before the mudarib share and shared with shareholders; IRR after the mudarib share, in IAH equity, usable only for IAH investment losses — GN-3 ¶20/25-27, IFSB-30 ¶256) and getting the sequence wrong changes every number downstream, so it must be owned in ONE place. Cross-area coordination needed.
BNM ¶13.5 forbids smoothing/DCR outright. Any PER/IRR interaction with this portfolio must be feature-flagged off per jurisdiction, which is a platform concern this entry does not express.

minAverageRatingNotch assumes an institution-internal integer scale. Mapping agency ratings onto it is configuration this entry does not model, and whether a conventional credit rating is an appropriate input at all was not researched.

Performance attribution, duration/profit-rate sensitivity and stress testing are absent. Modelling profit-rate duration for sukuk raises a prior question (whether a conventional rate-sensitivity measure is the right frame) that was not researched.
serviceDomains.summary: A managed portfolio of sukuk holdings with a mandate. The Islamic content is concentrated in three places: the funding pool is explicit on both the portfolio and every position (AAOIFI FAS 47, Transfer of Assets between Investment Pools, is research-confirmed by title and pool-boundary integrity is the rule it implies); the management basis is Mudarabah / Wakala / Proprietary with an exact profit-share ratio and a contractual ceiling; and non-compliance carries a divestment deadline and a purification computation with a named method authority.

uncertain: TAWARRUQ ITSELF IS CONTESTED AND THIS ENTRY DOES NOT ADJUDICATE IT. Organised Tawarruq is the subject of well-known adverse resolutions by some fiqh bodies while remaining standard interbank practice in several markets. This research retrieved NO Tawarruq-specific standard, so there is no rule here that passes judgement on the structure. What the rules do instead is make the structure's integrity checkable: did the bank take possession, did it bear risk, did the legs happen in the right order, is the price fixed. If an SSB rules the structure impermissible, that is a policy decision above this service domain, not a rule inside it.

The deferred sale price's presence in the enum does not establish that a Tawarruq commodity sale is a genuine sale rather than a form. The commodityPlatform field records which market facility was used; it is not evidence of a real commodity market.

The ribawi (gold/silver) rule in ISB-IMD-09 has no primary citation and is therefore a flag. If the owner obtains the clause, it can be promoted to a reject by changing one field in this entry — which is the point of keeping rules as data.

Early settlement rebate (ibra') is NOT modelled. A rebate on early settlement of a fixed deferred price is common and its permissibility and whether it may be contractually promised are both contested. Adding an ibra' field without a named authority would be inventing a compliance claim.

Direction (Placement/Taking) changes which party's possession must be evidenced, but the rules as written check the bank's possession on the SpotPurchase leg regardless. For a Taking the counterparty is the one taking possession first, so ISB-IMD-06 is too strong in that direction. This is a real modelling gap: it should become two rules gated on `direction`, and is left flagged here rather than silently fixed with an unverified assumption about who evidences what.

Netting of offsetting interbank Murabaha deals is not modelled. Set-off against a customer account 'requires the same currency or the prevailing rate (SS 3 §2/5/3)' per the research, which suggests netting needs its own rules; none are asserted.
serviceDomains.summary: Interbank liquidity placed and taken through commodity Murabaha (Tawarruq) instead of an interest-bearing deposit. The design is built around the one clause this research actually supports for the structure: Murabaha sequencing must show possession and risk transfer BEFORE the onward sale. So the legs are a first-class, ordered sub-resource with per-leg titleTransferred and riskBorneByBank, and the sequencing rule compares the ordinal of the spot purchase against the ordinal of the onward sale. The deferred sale price is a fixed total with cost and profit disclosed separately and an explicit accruesOnArrears = false invariant.

Second, the record's own claims are made mutually checkable: an arrangement that calls itself unilateral cannot also bind both parties. That is an internal contradiction and is rejected; every contested Shariah position is flagged.

uncertain: NO SCREENING THRESHOLD IS HARDCODED ANYWHERE IN THIS ENTRY, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN, NOT AN OMISSION. The frequently quoted 30/30/5 numbers appear in this fragment only inside rule EXAMPLES, as illustrative test data. Baking them into the schema would be asserting an authority the research explicitly says was not obtained.

The debt-ratio denominator basis (trailing-12-month average market cap vs spot market cap vs total assets) genuinely differs between published methodologies and flips borderline securities. It is modelled as a required enum with an authority; this agent does not know which is correct and does not pretend to.

The prohibited-activity category enum is a modelled set. Whether hotels, music/cinema, defence or conventional insurance belong on it differs between methodologies, and several methodologies subdivide further. Treat the enum as configuration surface and expect an SSB to amend it.

The purification formula is absent by design. Published sources conflict on per-share impermissible income vs a ratio over received dividends plus realised gains, and on whether capital gains are purified at all. The entry carries purificationRatioBps plus a REQUIRED method authority and formula reference, and computes nothing.

SECTOR CODE IS A COARSE PROXY AND THE SAME FAILURE MODE AS MCC APPLIES. The research warns about MCC: 'a mixed merchant carries one code ... Never present an MCC pass as a halal determination.' A single GICS or ICB code on a diversified issuer has the identical weakness. This is exactly why dataCoverageBps, the Refer outcome and ISB-EQS-04 exist, and why a sector code alone can never produce a Pass here.

Screening of SUKUK as opposed to equities reuses this domain only via complianceSourceRef on a holding. A sukuk screen asks different questions (the underlying asset, the obligor, the structure) and arguably needs its own control record. Reported as a gap rather than stretched to fit.
No look-through for funds, holding companies or index constituents. A fund's or conglomerate's own holdings are not screened, so a Pass on the parent says nothing about the subsidiaries.

Effective-dating is modelled as thresholdsEffectiveFrom/To on the snapshot plus an append-only reviewHistory. A true bi-temporal model (what did we believe, as at when) is stronger and is not implemented.
serviceDomains.summary: One screening result per security, with the screen itself carried as DATA. The design answer to the area guidance is this: the SSB-approved thresholds are SNAPSHOTTED onto every result (so the verdict is replayable), the method authority and source reference are REQUIRED fields, and the rules refuse a result whose authority is missing. Three outcomes only — Pass, Fail, Refer — because the research is explicit that there must be a referral path and never a silent pass. Every ratio is exact integer basis points; the denominator basis is an explicit enum because published sources genuinely differ on it and it changes the answer.

uncertain: standardRef's enum contains ONLY the AAOIFI/IFSB references this estate's research verified (FAS 35 risk reserves, FAS 39 zakah reporting, FAS 45 quasi-equity, FAS 47 pool transfers, FAS 30, IFSB GN-3). AAOIFI's full FAS series is much larger and the takaful FAS standards in particular were NEVER obtained — so every takaful posting will carry standardRef OTHER plus a prose note until a reviewer supplies the clause. That is deliberate: an enum value I cannot cite would be a fabricated citation.

FAS 1 (general presentation and disclosure) is the standard that would normally govern the chart of accounts and accountClass taxonomy, and it is NOT in this estate's research. accountClass (including the QUASI_EQUITY member, which FAS 45 does support) is therefore partly my construction.

The PER-before / IRR-after ordering (ISB-AFA-06, ISB-AFA-07) is well cited, but PER/IRR ITSELF is a jurisdictional fork, not a feature: AAOIFI SS 46 §6/6 permits it and IFSB GN-3 documents it, while BNM PD 028-63 ¶13.5 says the IFI 'must not implement profit smoothing practices or displaced commercial risk (DCR) techniques'. The generator must emit these rules behind a jurisdiction flag; hard-coding either position makes the product unshippable in half the market.

'accountCode startsWith PER' in ISB-AFA-06/07 is the one assert that depends on a naming convention rather than a typed field. If the template cannot support startsWith, the right fix is a reserveType enum column, not a looser rule.

I did NOT model the profit-distribution computation (pool income, weightages, mudarib share, provisional-to-final revision). That is the Deposits and Investment Accounts area's Profit Calculation And Distribution domain. This domain only asserts that whatever it computes posts legally.

What happens to a posting whose screening outcome is BLOCK AFTER it was already booked (an outcome arriving late) — reverse it, freeze it, or refer it — is not modelled. uncertain: The guaranteed/at-risk SPLIT is arithmetic I invented. In practice the at-risk amount of a Mudarabah IAH balance is not a stored number but a consequence of the pool's performance at a valuation date, and whether any part of a Mudarabah balance is ever 'guaranteed' (e.g. an unpaid declared-profit amount that has become a debt of the bank) is exactly the kind of question only an SSB can settle. I modelled declared profit as guaranteed-and-withdrawable and accrued profit as neither; a reviewer may disagree with the first half.

ISB-IBA-06 forbids accrued profit in every BOOKED and AVAILABLE balance type. That is my reading of 'undeclared profit is not yours'. The alternative industry practice — showing an indicative accrual as part of a booked balance with a disclaimer — is common and I rejected it as misleading. This is a judgement call, flagged as such.

PER/IRR SHARE as a balance component assumes the holder has an attributable share of the reserves. Whether an IAH's PER share is their property while in the reserve, and what happens to it on account closure, is a known-contested area; AAOIFI and BNM do not agree even on whether the reserve may exist.

I did not model multi-currency accounts (OBIE's Balance.Amount.SubType BCUR/LCUR hints at it). ISB-IBA-08's uniqueness key includes currency, so the schema permits it, but no rule governs how a multi-currency Islamic account's at-risk split behaves across currencies — and FX on a capital-at-risk pool raises its own Shariah questions I could not model.

The 'withdrawable' flag per component is mine and has no standard behind it. It exists because a single OBIE 'available' number cannot be honest, and a reviewer should check it against the actual withdrawal terms of each product rather than accept it as modelled.

uncertain: The AAOIFI Financial Accounting Standards that govern how IAH profit, PER/IRR and purification are PRESENTED were never obtained by this estate's research (DECISIONS.md WAVE 3 says so for takaful; the same is true here). Every money field on this statement is therefore a presentation choice, not a standard-backed line item. This is the single biggest gap in my slice.

Zakat: I carry only zakatAssessmentRef and no zakat figure. Whether a statement must disclose a zakat base or a zakat deducted amount is jurisdictional (compulsory collection in some jurisdictions, voluntary elsewhere) and I could not model it from verified sources. ISB-IST has no zakat rule as a result — a deliberate omission, not an oversight.

ISB-IST-02 assumes every balance movement is explained by a statement line in the same period. Value-dated postings that book in one period and value in another break this, and I did not model which of bookingAt or valueDate governs period membership. That choice changes the arithmetic of ISB-IST-01 and ISB-IST-02 and a reviewer must fix it before either rule is generated.

I modelled gross pool profit as an OPTIONAL disclosure (grossPoolProfitDisclosedMinor). Whether an IAH is entitled to see the pool's gross result — and not only their own share — is exactly the kind of transparency question IFSB-30 Principle 18 addresses and I could not resolve from the extracted text.

The OBIE statement surface has published code sets for Fee, Interest, Benefit, Value, Rate and Amount types, and NONE of them has a profit, purification, ta'widh or zakat member. I did not pick a UK.OBIE.* code to approximate any of them: unlike AccountTypeCode (where a value is mandatory and some code must be chosen), these are optional, so the honest action is to omit them from the OBIE response entirely and serve them on the sibling. A reviewer may prefer approximation plus disclosure; I chose omission.

AAOIFI SS 13 (Revised) (the capital provider bears capital loss)
AAOIFI SS 45
DESIGN.md §7

A NAV or a market value with no source and no timestamp cannot be disclosed to a holder as the worth of their units. 'flag' because an internally declared NAV may legitimately have no external source — which is itself worth seeing in the audit ledger.

AAOIFI SS 21 (Financial Paper — Shares and Bonds) governs screening; the estate's own 'Income Purification' domain owns the computation. NOTE: SS 21's screening THRESHOLDS could not be verified against primary text by this estate's research (DECISIONS.md WAVE 3), so no threshold appears in this rule — only the consequence of an outcome a versioned criteria set produced.
Unrealised movement is not income and not withdrawable. The enforcing rule is ISB-IBA-06 at the balance layer; this flag makes the position-level cause visible in the same ledger.
AAOIFI SS 13 (Revised) §8/1 (entitlement is to a share of REALISED profit)
Mixed unit scales inside one position make ISB-IPS-01's sum meaningless. One scale per position, fixed at open.
A closed position holding units, or carrying a live rahn, is an orphaned customer entitlement.
DESIGN.md §5.1 / §6 — the minor-unit exponent follows the currency; a position in a currency its account does not carry cannot be converted or summed safely.
Rahn over more than the position is worth is either a modelling error or a double pledge. A pledged holding is also not freely redeemable, which the available balance must reflect.
Writing capital loss down against a guaranteed (Qard/Wadiah) balance would pass the bank's loss to a depositor whose principal is guaranteed.

uncertain: AAOIFI SS 21's screening thresholds (commonly quoted as 30/30/5) could not be verified against primary text by this estate's research, and sources disagree on the purification formula. I therefore modelled NO threshold and NO formula: screening carries a versioned, SSB-approved criteria-set reference and an outcome. A generator default here would be manufacturing authority.

Unit accounting at a declared integer scale is my invention for keeping floats out. It is correct arithmetic but I do not know whether it matches how Islamic banks actually express fractional IAH units, or whether a ratio pair would be the better representation for a unitised holding. A reviewer should check this against a real IAH product before it is generated.

Whether an IAH position should be published to TPPs at all is an open product/privacy question. I mapped the whole domain to the sibling surface, but a holdings list is materially more sensitive than a balance, and AIS v4.0.1 has no holdings resource to normalise it against.

IJARA_ASSET_INTEREST is in instrumentKind because a lessee's interest in a leased asset is a real position, but I modelled no asset-specific field (residual value, transfer-of-ownership schedule for IMB). That belongs to the Ijara Muntahia Bittamleek product domain, and I may have the boundary in the wrong place.

Corporate actions on sukuk (early call, restructuring, default/sukuk-holder recourse to the underlying asset) are folded into one CORPORATE_ACTION movement kind. Sukuk default and recourse are a serious modelling area I did not attempt.

I did not model the relationship between a position's valuation and the Balance domain's at-risk split — i.e. whether atRiskAmountMinor must equal the sum of position carrying amounts. It probably must, and a cross-domain rule would be the right place to say so, but the assert grammar has no cross-domain aggregate and I did not invent one.

It is therefore the clearest justification for DESIGN.md §7 RULE 3's sibling server — a unitised Mudarabah holding is simply not an Open Banking AIS resource.
the only thing about a position that OBIE can express is which account it belongs to
A position's carrying value COULD be published as an INFO balance. I do NOT recommend it: an unlabelled informational number next to a CLAV balance invites a TPP to add them together.
